# island-simulator Development Plan

## Document purpose

This is the living execution ledger for the original roughly 300-hour development campaign. On
2026-10-12 the operator set approximately 100 productive hours as the target implementation window
for the remaining plan. This is a planning target, not an automatic stop: work continues until the
operator stops it. The requested functional scope is retained, but initial visual fidelity and
iteration depth should fit that target. If the functional plan finishes early, use the remaining
time to deepen individual items toward the quality of the former roughly 400-hour outlook. This is
not a feature wish list: checked
items require the validation named by their phase, and platform claims must be supported by actual
runtime evidence. New discoveries, regressions, framework workarounds, asset provenance work, and
deferred polish belong here as soon as they become material.

Status markers:

- `[x]` completed and evidenced
- `[ ]` not completed
- `[~]` in progress
- `[!]` blocked or degraded, with the reason written next to the item

## Latest lighting pass — directional sun shadow map

The operator's 2026-10-19 evening backlog opens with real directional shadows. `SunShadowMap`
(`docs/large-object-shadows.md`) renders one orthographic fixed-sun depth map, 144 m square around
the camera on an 8 m anchor grid, so it is rebuilt only when the camera leaves a cell; every
caster is static. Canopy trees, snags, understory, bushes, living and broken palms, the hut, the
wreck hull and the opaque helicopter airframe cast; terrain (with its cave and stream patches),
grass, all jungle plant surfaces and palms receive, multiplying by the same `uCanopyAmbient` tone
the baked field used, while the baked field keeps only 45% of its darkening as sky occlusion.
Depth is packed into an RGBA8 target and read through a plain `sampler2D` with four bilinearly
blended point taps, honouring EasyGL's `uRtFlipV` flag, so WebGL 2, GLES 3 and desktop GL share
one path. The three projected footprint shadows are disabled while the map is active; contact
patches and animal grounding remain. Resolution is 2048 px on desktop and 1024 px on Web/Android.

Inspected native evidence: `20261019T185824Z-jungle` (snag and crown shadows lie on the slope in
the sun's direction and attach at the trunk bases), `-hut` (tree shadows cross the clearing and the
hut casts its own), `-helicopter`, `-shipwreck`, `-east`; the sweep overview, beach, grass, litter,
west, palms, campfire, monkeys, goats, boars, bear and cave all pass their gates. The jungle frame
reports 923 casters in one map render. The first 2x2 comparison showed stepped frond-shadow edges on
the beach (`20261019T192548Z-movement`); receivers now blend a 4x4-texel weighted comparison, and
the recaptured movement frame shows the same palm shadows with edges softening over about two
texels. Chrome 155/SwiftShader `20261019T190321.794405Z-chrome-helicopter` passes all three views
with the 1024 px map rendering 873--877 casters, no caster shader failures, GL error zero and live
contexts. All 73 active native tests pass. Remaining: animals, hut and wreck surfaces and water do
not yet receive; rotor blades and glass do not cast; a physical-GPU FPS comparison is the operator's.

## Quad bike pass 3 (2026-10-20) — the engine left idling, the tyres heard

The engine now starts when the rider gets on and idles on after the rider steps off, heard
from where the quad stands (fading over 60 m), its exhaust still smoking and its lamps still
lit, until it is switched off a minute and a half later or the quad lies on its side.
`QuadBike::SlideSpeed` reports how fast the touching tyres slide sideways (the fastest, over
the last step), and a procedural tyre loop (a low rumble under a crunch of grains: 1800 short
dull clicks over two seconds) plays louder and higher with the rolling speed and much louder
in a skid or a power slide; heard close while riding, from where the quad is otherwise. Core
checks: the tyres hardly slide rolling straight and skid in a full-lock turn at speed; the
loop is an audible two seconds.

## Quad bike pass 2 (2026-10-20) — ruts, dust, spray and knocks

What the wheels leave and throw. A core `TyreTrackField` lays a piece of rut every third of a
metre behind each wheel rolling on sand or soil (none on rock or under water), as wide as the
tyre and pressed deeper under load; the ground keeps them five minutes, the wet sand at the
water's edge one (480 pieces, the oldest giving way). `TyreTrackRenderer` draws each piece as a
terrain-conforming rut, darker inside soft lips, with the knobs' staggered prints across it
within 22 m, alpha-blended beside the footprints, to 42 m. A core `WheelThrowField` (two
instances): dust off dry sand and coastal soil (the forest floor only after a dry spell, none
in the wet), from 2 m/s, more with the speed and from the driven rear wheels, hanging in the
quad's wake, swelling, settling and drifting downwind within 1.8 s; spray in water deeper
than 3 cm, flung up and back and falling within 0.8 s (each 96 puffs, drawn as dust puffs in
sand and foam colours). `QuadBike::LastImpact` reports the hardest knock of a step (the speed
into a tree or rock, of the chassis meeting the ground, or of a wheel's travel bottoming out),
and from 2 m/s, or on a rollover, the soundscape plays a procedural knock (a sagging body
thump, the crack of the plastic and a second knock, a rattle of loose metal), louder and deeper
the harder it is. A new QA view `quad-drive` sets off up the beach path from the south shore
on a fixed clock (32 updates of 0.1 s) with the chase camera following: 39 km/h, 100 rut
pieces and the dust behind. Core checks: ruts per third of a metre on sand, none on rock,
short-lived on wet sand; dust at speed only, spray only in water; a tree knocks hard, the flat
does not.

## Quad bike pass 1 (2026-10-20) — ride a utility quad over the island

Operator request: an ATV to ride, switched to and from walking by a key, with a CNA avatar on
it, as realistic as possible, with engine sound, exhaust smoke, lights at night (and by day),
rolling over and set back on its wheels with Backspace, at a real quad's top speed. The core
`QuadBike` (previous commit) is the physics: a 260 kg rigid body on four sprung, damped wheels,
tyre grip by surface (sand 0.75, wet sand 0.85, soil 1.0, steep ground 1.05, rock 1.3, the
seabed 0.7, a quarter less when the weather has wet the ground), a CVT drive to the rear, a
governor at 80 km/h, brakes on all four, speed-sensitive steering and hull contacts that let it
roll. Its body frame now puts x on the rider's right (forward x up): in the right-handed world
that frame is mirrored (the renderer's body matrix reflects), and the core check now asserts
that steering right turns it right; before, A and D were swapped.

In the game the quad stands parked in a clear, level spot near the hut. F mounts it (from more
than 9 m away it is brought three and a half metres ahead of the walker) and dismounts on the
left, the right or behind, wherever the ground is clear; W/S throttle and brake or reverse, A/D
steer, Space is the handbrake, Backspace rights it. A chase camera rides 4.8 m behind and 1.9 m
up, never below the ground; the mouse swings it round the quad and it settles back behind 1.5 s
after the mouse rests. The walker's position follows the quad, so the wildlife and the sounds
follow the rider. Obstacles (trunks, rocks, the hut) push it back through the collision grid.

The model (`QuadBikeRenderer`, 16 688 triangles, five static draws and one dynamic): a steel
frame; moulded fenders swept round the wheels (crowned tops, turned-down outer lips, deeper
inner skirts, carried down into the floorboards); a hood rolling over into a fascia with a
grille and two wide headlamps; a rear deck into a rear face with the taillight; ribbed
floorboards with toe and heel guards; mud flaps; front and rear racks; a black brush guard and
a rear grab bar; side panels; a tank with its filler cap; a long seat; a finned engine, the
exhaust header, a muffler under the right rear fender and its tip; a skid plate; bars under a
pod that turn with the steering; knobby tyres (two staggered tread rows and shoulder knobs) on
five-spoke rims that spin and steer; A-arms, coil-over shocks, the swingarm and its mono-shock
following each wheel's travel. One material shader with paint, plastic, rubber, steel, chrome
and lens responses, fog and the sun shadow map. Its own shadow is drawn on the ground plane
under it: a soft occlusion under the body and each tyre (also by night and under cloud) and the
silhouette (with the rider's stand-in figure) cast along the sun, flat and even (the film
writes a depth rounded to a coarse step, so overlapping layers of the silhouette fail the
strict test instead of darkening twice).

The rider is a CNA GamerServices avatar (a man of 1.78 m, red jersey) loaded asynchronously and
posed in code: leaning to the bars, thighs forward on the seat, shins down to the floorboards,
the hands turned palm down with all three joints of every finger curled round the grips; the
shoulders turn and the elbows fold with the bars. The avatar needs `CNA_ENABLE_NET` in the
pinned CNA (`ISLAND_CNA_AVATAR`, on for desktop) and its 288 bone uniform vectors exceed GLES
3's guarantee, so the Web and Android builds draw a simple stand-in rider, as does the desktop
until the avatar has loaded.

The engine sound: two procedural loops of a big single (2200 and 5600 rpm: a bark of resonant
noise per firing over its harmonics, valvetrain clatter, drive whine), crossfaded and
pitch-shifted by the revs the CVT model gives, louder with the throttle; heard close while
riding. The exhaust: puffs from the tip, more and denser with the throttle, carried with the
quad's speed, swelling, rising and drifting downwind, gone within 2.4 s (drawn as grey dust
puffs before the night grade).

The headlights: two lamp lenses that glow (an additive glare after the grade, larger at night;
the red taillight at night) whenever the quad is ridden, by day too. At night the beam lights
the ground through the grade itself: the frame's alpha is set to one, then a slab over the pool
ahead is drawn depth-tested, each of its pixels finding where its view ray comes down to the
ground and how strongly the lamps light it there (a 20-degree core and a softer spill, falling
off with distance to 40 m, facing the lamps), and writing one minus that into the alpha only;
the grade then multiplies each pixel by the hour's colour plus that light, so lit grass, plants
and ground keep their own colours instead of the night's blue (lit within the 8-bit frame
before the grade, they could never exceed the grade's dark blue). The slab is drawn nearer
along the eye's rays but never before the lamps, so the quad and its rider stand in front of it
and stay unlit, and what stands in the pool lower than the eye is lit.

QA views: `quad` (parked, from the front left), `quad-ride` (ridden with the bars turned right,
from the front right), `quad-chase` (the chase camera); all pass natively by day, and at 21:30
for `quad-ride` and `quad-chase`. Core checks: the right turn, the engine loops' firing rates,
the exhaust smoking at idle and more with the throttle, drifting downwind and clearing.
Not yet: dust and spray from the wheels, tyre tracks in the sand, a crash sound.

## Weather pass 1 (2026-10-20) — clear, cloudy, overcast, showers and thunderstorms

The second half of the operator's request. A core `WeatherSystem` chains spells of 1.5 to 5
game hours (clear, partly cloudy, overcast, showers, thunderstorm) through a transition table
in which fair weather clouds over and showers clear or build into a storm, never fair weather
straight into a storm or back, from a seed (a run repeats), each spell eased into the next:
cloud cover, rain (showers come and go within their spell), wind, ground wetness (soaked in
about a minute of heavy rain, dry a few minutes after) and, in a storm, lightning every 5-22
real seconds with the strike's distance for the thunder. Snow is deliberately absent (not
possible on a tropical island at sea level; the operator asked). `ApplyTo` folds it into the
hour's light: overcast weakens the sun's shadows (85 %), hides its disc, dims and greys the
scene and turns the sky to a grey that keeps the hour's brightness, and hides the stars. Core
checks: repeatable, spells bounded, no illegal jumps, twenty game days bring rain and a storm,
the former partly cloudy weather changes nothing, a storm soaks the ground and strikes,
overcast weakens shadows and dims, the names parse and there is no snow.

In the game the weather starts partly cloudy and runs with the clock; the fixed QA views keep
it unless `--weather` asks for one, so every existing capture is unchanged (`hut` 0.1 % by 20
levels); Y steps through the weathers (after a thunderstorm the spells run on their own
again). The shared cumulus shade takes a coverage uniform (unset it reads 0, the former
quarter), so the cloud shadows on land and sea close up under overcast; the sky draws a grey
cloud deck that closes with the cover and darkens in the rain; the terrain darkens by up to
30 % where it is wet (on land only); rain falls as world-anchored streaks on a 1.2 m world grid
around the walker (three drops a cell at full rain, 8.5 m/s, slanted with the wind, faded at
the edges of a 26 m by 22 m volume, never in the cave, the bunker or under the sea) before the
night grade; lightning adds a brief additive flash; the soundscape plays a procedural rain
loop by the rain's strength and, after each strike's distance over the speed of sound, a near
crack-and-roll or a distant roll of thunder. Native `hut` (partly cloudy, overcast, showers,
thunderstorm) and `flight` (showers, and a thunderstorm at 21:00) pass. Not yet: stronger
gust fronts with the wind, morning mist, rain rings on the water.

## Day/night pass 1 (2026-10-20) — the island's clock, the moving sun, the night and the moon

Operator request: day and night with the moon, 24 game hours in about 24 minutes, then weather.
A core `DayNightCycle` keeps the clock (1440 real seconds a day) and gives the light of any
hour: the sun on an equinox path whose latitude (17.94 degrees) and east axis (8.99 degrees)
are fitted so that at 14:00 it stands exactly where the former fixed sun did (the core check
compares it to `environment::SunDirection` within 0.001), rising at 06:00 and setting at 18:00;
a moon that trails the sun by its phase through an 8-day lunar month (full opposite the sun);
the scene grade (full day above 20 degrees, a golden hour, a rose-violet dusk to -6, a dark
blue night lifted by the moon), the sky's zenith and horizon colours, the shadow strength and
the stars. Core checks: the fit, sunrise and sunset at six, the noon height, daylight at
14:00, a dark starry midnight, the full moon high at midnight, under 4 % change per game minute
(3.3 % at the dusk), 24 real minutes to a day, a held clock.

In the game the clock runs from 14:00, or from `--time-of-day`, and is held still for every
fixed QA view and smoke run, so every existing capture is unchanged at 14:00 (`hut` 0.12 % of
pixels by 20 levels, the wind; `campfire` 0 %). T moves it an hour on. Each frame `sun_light`
publishes the hour: the eight `uToSun` uploads (terrain, grass, jungle, palms, props, wreck,
cave, ocean), the monkeys' skinning shader and the animals' shared CPU light direction take
its shading direction (the sun by day, the moon by night, blended through the dusk, never
under 15 degrees so no shadow term divides by a vanishing sun height; scaled to the former
constant's length so 14:00 uploads it exactly); the sun shadow map follows it, re-rendering
when it has turned a quarter of a degree, its shadows scaled by the hour's strength (none at
night) and the cumulus shade only dimming sunlight. A new `TimeOfDayRenderer` multiplies the
drawn scene by the grade (a blend-factor multiply, skipped at full day) before the campfire's
flames, then draws 1100 stars and a phased moon (lit on the side facing the sun, pale by day,
faded through its rising, with a halo) depth-tested behind the land. The sky shader takes the
hour's zenith and horizon (divided by the grade it is multiplied by afterwards) and hides the
sun's disc as it sets. The campfire's light now survives the grade and at night lights the
ground's own colours warm instead of adding a flat glow; its smoke, drawn after the grade,
takes the hour's darkness and a low orange glow. Captures take `--time-of-day`; a reviewed
`night-scene` validation profile applies only to an explicit hour with the sun 4 degrees or
more below the horizon (18:18-05:42) and still fails a black or featureless frame (unit test).
Native `hut` at 14:00, 17:00 (long shadows), 18:24 (dusk), 21:00, 00:00 and 19:00, `flight` at
21:00 (a moonlit sea) and 05:48 (dawn), and `campfire` at 14:00 and 21:00 pass. Still on the
fixed 14:00 sun: lighting baked into geometry at build time (terrain vertex colours, the hut,
jetty, bridge, lookout, helicopter, wreck, campfire stones, twigs, the canopy light field,
the static contact shadows); hidden at night, but at the golden hours their shading faces the
afternoon. A `--game-day` switch sets the day and with it the moon's phase: the `flight` view
at 02:50 on day 3 shows the 88 % gibbous moon low over the sea with its glitter path on the
water (the ocean's glints follow the shading direction, the moon at night), stars and moonlit
clouds. The moon draws over the sky shader's cumulus rather than behind them (open). Next:
weather.

## Loop pass 283 (2026-10-21) — house geckos at the lantern

On tropical islands the geckos come out on the walls by any light at night to hunt the
insects it draws. Two now do so on the hut's front wall beside the lantern (whose moths pass
258 added): `hut_geckos::At` (header-only, deterministic in the clock) gives each a cycle of
19 or 25 s: it rests at its spot on the boards, creeps 0.3-0.4 m towards the light over 6 s with
its tail twitching, darts 6 cm at a moth and back, licks its lips, rests, and creeps home. They
fade in from dusk (the lantern's darkness above 0.45) and are gone by day. `GeckoState` gains
an optional wall normal: on a wall the gecko's frame is built on the wall's plane (its up the
normal, its heading turned from straight up the wall), on the ground nothing changes; the
shared insect batch makes room for the two. About 17 cm nose to tail (tokay-sized), tan and
brown. A probe at four times the size showed both on the boards below the lantern, the right
way round; at their real size they are a detail to find walking up to the hut at night.
`hut` at 21:30 and by day and `geckos` pass, and the tests.

## Loop pass 282 (2026-10-21) — the Milky Way

Far from any lights, a tropical island's moonless night shows the Milky Way arching over it;
the sky had only its 1100 stars. `TimeOfDayRenderer` now builds a fixed band along a great
circle tilted to arch to 63 degrees (180 segments by 10 rows, about 20 degrees wide and wider
towards its core): its brightness falls off softly across the band, is mottled into star clouds
by two scales of value noise wrapped round the ring, split by a dark dust rift that wanders
across the band and is deepest near the core, and is brightest and warmest at the core (44
degrees up) and bluish-white along the arms; low down it is lost in the haze. 600 fainter stars
are crowded into it, half near the core and half along the arc above the horizon. It is drawn
additively under the stars and fades with the stars' visibility (the clouds and the dawn) and
far sooner than them with the moon (by 90 % of the moonlight). A first strength put its core
only 9 levels above the night sky; it now stands about 15 above. `palms` at 23:00 on a moonless
day 8 shows the soft arch rising behind the crowns; on day 4 the moonlit sky washes it out;
`flight` passes too. The field stars and their diagnostic are unchanged.

## Loop pass 281 (2026-10-21) — the shore's foam no longer reads as a dashed line

From the air (`headland` at sunset) the breaking foam along the beach read as a dashed white
road marking: evenly spaced runs with even gaps. The crest is broken up by a mask, and that
mask was one world-space sine (about 7.1 m wavelength, gently warped), so along a straight
beach its gaps repeated every 7 m. It is now the sum of three incommensurate wavelengths (7.1,
13.4 and 3.2 m, the shortest warped too), each drifting at its own pace, normalised to the same
range so the foam's overall coverage is unchanged: the runs and gaps come in uneven lengths.
`headland` at 18:12 shows irregular runs where the dashes were; `jetty` and `beach` close up
pass and look as before.

## Loop pass 280 (2026-10-21) — a storm tears leaves loose and shakes the coconuts down

The gust fronts already came faster in a storm (pass 234), but each front shed leaves and
coconuts as in the trade wind. `CanopyLeafFallField::SetWind` and `FallingFruitField::SetWind`
now take the weather's wind: a front tears a leaf from a crown with the chance times the wind's
square (every crown in range from 1.58; a shower's 1.35 almost doubles it), the leaves are
carried downwind by the square of the wind too (3.6 m/s in a storm's 2) on a wider rock, and
a front shakes a nut from a fruiting palm with up to four times the chance. New core checks:
over five minutes in the densest stand 105 leaves in the trade wind against 288 in a storm,
carried up to 71 m and 129 m downwind; from a row of eight palms in twenty minutes 20 coconuts
against 68. In the trade wind nothing changes; the tests and `jungle` in a thunderstorm pass.

## Loop pass 279 (2026-10-21) — rain splashes on the ground

Heavier rain now splashes on the land round the walker as the sea's rings already showed it
on the water: a new `RainSplashRenderer` keeps a fixed world grid of 0.4 m cells out to 9 m,
each taking a drop every 0.45-1.05 s (its own period and phase, a fresh spot in the cell each
time) when the rain is heavy enough (none below 0.3, every cell in a downpour of 0.8 and up);
the drop throws a small crown of four droplets that fly out at 0.55-0.9 m/s and up at
0.8-1.1 m/s and fall back within 0.16 s, drawn as short pale streaks about a pixel wide,
faded with their age and towards the edge of the radius. Not on the sea or the swash (they
have the rings), world-anchored, before the night grade with the rain. `campfire` and `beach`
in a thunderstorm show the ground seething with small splashes between the puddle rings;
`beach` in showers passes too.

## Loop pass 278 (2026-10-21) — the forest and the grass in a storm's wind

As the palms (pass 277), the forest trees and the grass now answer the weather's wind
(`uStormWind`: the wind's direction and strength). Above the trade wind the crowns sway up to
1.7 times as far and lean downwind in world space (by up to about half a metre at the crowns'
highest wind weight, 0.9, in a storm's wind of 2), tossing on their own beat and pressed further by each gust front;
the grass blades whip up to twice as far and lie over downwind by 6-11 % of their height,
flattened by the gusts. In the trade wind nothing changes. `grass` and `jungle` calm and
`jungle` in a thunderstorm pass; `grass` in a thunderstorm fails the luminance floor as a dark
scene under the trees, and fails the same way without this change (checked by capturing it
with the change stashed), like `jetty-end` in a storm.

## Loop pass 277 (2026-10-21) — palms blown in a storm's wind

The palms swayed the same in a storm as in the trade wind (only the gust fronts came faster).
Their vertex shader now takes the weather's wind with the wind's direction (`uStormWind`):
above the trade wind (1, a shower's 1.35, a storm's 2) the fronds sway up to 1.8 times as far,
and are blown downwind in world space by up to about 1.2 m at their tips in a storm, thrashing
(a faster per-frond beat) and pressed further by each passing gust front, sagging a little as
they go. The trunks stand (their wind weight is 0); in the trade wind nothing changes. `palms`
in a thunderstorm shows the crowns swept downwind; the calm and showers captures and the tests
pass. (The sun shadow casters stay unswayed, as before; in a storm the shadows are gone.)

## Loop pass 276 (2026-10-21) — the quad bike wet in the rain

The quad's material takes the weather's wetness too: its rough parts (the knobby tyres, the
black plastic, the seat vinyl, the stand-in rider's cloth) darken by up to 25 %, the metals and
the glossy paint not, and every surface carries a film of water that mirrors the sky at a
glancing view (the fresnel reflection's strength at least 0.55 of the wetness and up to 2.7
times as strong). `quad` in a thunderstorm shows the darker tyres and the wet sheen along the
red fenders against the dry `quad` overcast (no rain yet, so dry); all three captures and the
tests pass.

## Loop pass 275 (2026-10-21) — a closed sky under overcast and in a storm

A storm's sky showed blue-teal holes overhead and bluish cumulus smears along the horizon: the
grey cloud deck's threshold still left gaps at full cover where its sum of sines dipped low
(and let 6 % of the blue through everywhere), and the fair-weather cumulus masses, white-topped
with blue-grey bases, were drawn over the deck. The deck now closes completely as the cover
goes from a shower's 0.76 to an overcast's 0.86, keeping a faint light and dark texture from
its own field, and the cumulus masses fade out behind it over the same range. Showers keep
their broken sky with blue between the clouds. `palms` in a thunderstorm and overcast show a
closed grey deck, in showers the broken one; `birds` in a thunderstorm lost the teal smears;
`flight` overcast passes too. (Found looking at the pass-274 `palms` storm capture.)

## Loop pass 274 (2026-10-21) — the hut and the palms soak in the rain

The ground and the forest trees already darkened in the rain; the hut and the palms stayed
dry-looking. Both shaders now take the weather's wetness (`uWetness`): the hut's thatch goes up
to 38 % darker as it soaks, its weathered boards 17 % (the walls stand under the eaves), its
window glass not at all; the palms' grey bark goes 28 % darker and the fronds 10 %. `hut` and
`palms` in a thunderstorm show the dark wet thatch and trunks; dry, both are unchanged; all four
captures and the tests pass.

## Loop pass 273 (2026-10-21) — no rain under the hut's roof

The rain streaks fell straight through the hut's thatch onto the veranda and into the room.
`RainRenderer::SetShelter` now takes a gabled roof (its centre, its turn, the half-span out to
each eave, the half-length along the ridge and the heights of the eaves and the ridge), and no
drop is drawn below its slopes, tested in the roof's own frame; the game gives it the hut's
thatch (2.73 m out from the ridge, 2.32 m along it, 2.08 m above the floor at the eaves and
3.62 m at the ridge). With the eave drips (pass 272), the water now comes off the roof at its
edge instead of through it. A probe counted 24-28 drops a frame kept out from under the roof in
`hut` in a thunderstorm (of about 4350 drawn); the capture and the tests pass.

## Loop pass 272 (2026-10-21) — the hut's eaves drip in the rain

In rain the hut's thatch now sheds its water as a real roof does, off the drip edge: a new
`EaveDripRenderer` takes the tip of every leaf in the thatch's lowest row on both slopes (96
tips, from `BuildHutThatchBlade`), and from each lets up to three drops fall under gravity to
the ground below (their streaks lengthen with the speed, about 0.7 s for the 2.5 m fall),
splash in a small ring that spreads and thins over 0.14 s, then wait for the thatch to gather
the next. The harder it rains, the more of a tip's drops run and the shorter the waits, so a
shower drips and a downpour pours in near-curtains along the eaves. World-anchored, drawn with
the rain before the grade, out to 45 m. `hut` in a thunderstorm shows the drip line falling
past the side wall; `hut` in showers passes too.

## Loop pass 271 (2026-10-21) — wildlife takes shelter from the rain

The animals now take cover from the rain as they do from the dark. The day fliers (butterflies,
dragonflies, flies) drop out one by one from a light rain of 0.15 and are all in the leaves at
0.6, so most are gone in a shower's rain; the birds and the monkeys sit out a downpour (the
storm's rain above 0.5, full at 0.9; the shower's 0.55 hardly reaches it) through the same
path as the night: their nightness is the larger of the dark and the downpour, so the birds
take a perch apiece and the monkeys rest; and the fruit bats, which come out at night, stay
in their roost in a storm (only the few day fliers move). `butterflies` in showers shows the
meadow empty; `birds` and `monkeys` hold a staged animal for their close-ups and look as
before in a thunderstorm; all five weather captures and the tests pass.

## Loop pass 270 (2026-10-21) — the rain beats the campfire down

The campfire now answers the rain. A shared `weather_now::FireDousing()` is 0 when dry and in a
shower's light rain, rising smoothly through heavier rain (from 0.35) to 1 in a storm's
downpour. Doused, the flames stand half as tall, thin and sputter; the sparks go out; the
embers glow 45 % less and the wet ash goes dark; the low smoke turns to a whiter, denser steam
while the high plume thins; the firelight (the night's point light through the grade and the
warm light the terrain, grass and jungle shaders add round the pit, now scaled by a shared
`uCampfireStrength` uniform) falls to 40 %; and the crackle falls by 45 %. Dry, `campfire` is
unchanged; a shower's rain (0.55 at its heaviest) douses it at most 23 %; in a
thunderstorm by day and at 21:30 the low flames, the smaller light pool and the pale steam
show. All five captures pass. (The misplaced doc comment of `weather_now::SeaState` sat on
`AddMoonShadows`; it is back on its function.)

## Loop pass 269 (2026-10-21) — the resident's clothes soak in the rain

Out in the rain the resident's clothes and hair now darken as they soak, as wet cotton does:
the renderer takes the weather's wetness (1.2 times it, so a shower soon drenches them; it
rises with the rain and dries over the next few hours like the ground) and darkens the cloth by
up to 36 %, the hair by 30 %, the fibre belt and sandals by 24 % and the skin only by 5 %,
baked into the vertex colours with the rest of the lighting. `resident` in showers shows the
darker shirt and shorts against the skin; the dry day is unchanged (wetness 0).

## Loop pass 268 (2026-10-21) — dust in the forest's sunbeams

Under the trees the air now carries dust and pollen that glints where the sun comes through: a
new `SunbeamMoteRenderer` sets specks on a fixed 0.8 m world grid round the walker (about two
cells in three, 0.3-2.5 m above the ground, out to 8 m), each wandering slowly and turning so
it glints, lit only where the canopy light field lets the direct sun through to it and only
while the walker's own neighbourhood is shaded (the field's mean 5 m around below 0.98, full
below 0.78), so they show against the forest's shade and never in the open meadows or on the
beach. They are tiny warm additive discs (at least 1 cm, about 2 px at a distance), brightest
looking into the light because dust scatters forwards, and they fade with the distance and
with the direct sun (none at night or under overcast). A first gate wanted the neighbourhood
below 0.45 and never opened: the island's forest still passes 0.7-0.95 of the sun to its floor.
Probes showed about 35 motes in frame in `litter` and `ground-broadleaf` (soft specks against
the trunks); `jungle`, `beach` and `clearing-edge` stand in the open and show none. `litter`,
`hut`, `jungle`, `beach` and `ground-broadleaf` pass.

## Loop pass 267 (2026-10-21) — whitecaps in a strong wind

In a strong wind the open sea now breaks into scattered whitecaps: from a sea state of 1.15
(showers' wind) to full at 1.65 (a storm's), the ocean shader lays white crests where three
wave trains at uneven angles, through a slow warp, rise together on the steeper wave faces,
broken up by a finer train that its footprint filter calms with the distance, only over water
deeper than 3-9 m (not the lagoon flats) and fading out by 680 m. A first field (two sine waves
multiplied) set the caps in a visible regular grid; the third train and the warp scatter them.
`flight` in a thunderstorm shows them on the dark sea; the calm `jetty-end` is unchanged and
`water` and `jetty-end` in showers pass. (`jetty-end` in a thunderstorm still fails the colour
floor as before: a murky grey scene.)

## Loop pass 266 (2026-10-20) — moon shadows

A bright moon casts soft shadows, but the hour's shadow strength fell to nothing at night (the
core clock's own contract, checked by its tests). The game now adds the moon's
(`weather_now::AddMoonShadows`, after the weather): 40 % of the moonlight (which carries the
phase, the moon's height and the clouds' cover) while the sun is down, along the shading
direction that at night already follows the moon; the shadow map and every receiver take it,
and the direct-sun highlights it gates take the moon's faint share. Under a high full moon the
trees, the hut and the tower lay soft shadows; on a moonless or clouded night nothing changes.
`hut` and `flight` at 02:50 on day 3 (a full moon) pass; the day is unchanged.

## Loop pass 265 (2026-10-20) — a storm's surf breaks harder

The shoreline's breaking foam (the crest and the wash behind it) now follows the weather's sea
too (`uSeaState`, the same state that raises the waves): in a storm's 1.7 the crests run up to
1.2 times as full and the wash 1.7 times as white and wide, with a slightly higher ceiling; at
the trade wind's 1 nothing changes (the calm `jetty` is identical). `jetty` in a thunderstorm
shows the whiter surf. (The white lace lying on the flat sand some metres from the visible water
there is the swash over a few centimetres of water, too shallow for the sea's colour to show;
it was left as it is.)

## Loop pass 264 (2026-10-20) — whales offshore

Life on the open sea beyond the reef. A core `WhalePod` (a function of the clock, deterministic)
brings a humpback to the surface every 35-85 s somewhere 330-620 m out, swimming along the
coast at 1.6 m/s through a nine-second roll: it blows first (six mist puffs that stand up five
metres within a second, then spread, drift downwind and thin away over about five seconds),
then rolls its back up through the swell and under again, and one roll in three raises its
flukes as it sounds. `WhaleRenderer` draws the back as a 12 m half-ellipsoid with a pale belly
line and the small dorsal fin two-thirds back, the crest of the arc sliding toward the tail as
it goes down, and the broad flukes (dark above, pale beneath) with the tail stock; shaded by the
hour's light and hazed toward the fog colour with the distance, drawn before the sea so the
water covers what lies under it. The blow uses the cascade's mist renderer, which now takes a
far range (700 + 200 m) and a density for it. A probe build holding a back and a fluking whale
330-360 m in front of `jetty-end` showed both at the right scale, dark grey-blue on the far sea
(a first build drew them black; they are now lighter and hazed); the probe was removed. Core
check: in ten minutes 7-16 surfacings, all 320-640 m out, each blow standing up over 4 m and
gone within six seconds. `jetty-end`, `dolphins` and `overview` pass.

## Loop pass 263 (2026-10-20) — the hermit crabs keep to the night

Hermit crabs forage mostly at night. `HermitCrabGroup` takes the darkness (`SetNightness`; never
set in the tests): by day a pause lasts eight times as long, and after dark a forage runs up to
twice as long. Core check: over five minutes with no observer the crabs are paused in more than
half of the samples by day and in under half as many by night. `hermit-crabs` passes.

## Loop pass 262 (2026-10-20) — waiting out the rain; frogs after rain

Two small weather touches. In a downpour (rain above 0.6) the resident now waits it out
wherever they have stopped on their round (the pause is held, as at the fire at night) and
walks on when it eases. And the night chorus swells after rain: the crickets and frogs call up

damps them as before). Not yet heard by a person; the suite passes. (The `resident` QA view,
which stages the resident's walk and checks it, keeps them walking: forced into a thunderstorm
it failed the walk check until it was exempted; both now pass.)

## Loop pass 261 (2026-10-20) — the beach crabs go down at night

The beach's claw-waving crabs keep to the day. `CrabColony` takes the darkness (`SetNightness`;
never set in the tests, which keeps day and night alike): after dark each crab runs home to its
colony's burrow and goes down it, staying down until morning (the night keeps the all-clear from
counting), then emerges as after a fright. A first build left one colony's five crabs running
on the beach all night, 6-29 m from a burrow they could not reach; a crab that has not reached
its burrow after 20 s now digs in where it stands (these crabs dig their own holes) and comes

minute and a half. `crabs` (a daytime QA view) passes.

## Loop pass 260 (2026-10-20) — rain rings on the puddles

The puddles (Loop pass 233) lay still under falling rain. The terrain shader now rings them

a fresh point (each cell its own period of 0.9-1.7 s, a share of the strikes by the rain's
strength), its ring spreading to 12 cm and fading in the strike's period, a pale line at least
8 mm (and a pixel) wide; only where a ring is several pixels across (a ground footprint under
3.5 cm). A first build drew 1 cm rings too fine for the screen (under a pixel at a few metres);
a probe build forcing water over the hut's clearing showed the rings scattered over it; the
probe was removed. `hut` by day and in showers pass.

## Loop pass 259 (2026-10-20) — distant rain curtains

In showery and overcast weather, grey shafts of rain now hang from far showers over the sea
round the horizon (`TimeOfDayRenderer::DrawRainCurtains`): seven curtains at spread bearings,
drifting slowly round, each 0.2-0.3 radians wide and 6-10 degrees tall, in fourteen streaked
strips soft at the sides, faint where it hangs from the cloud, densest a little below and
thinning toward the sea, slanted with the wind, in the hour's horizon grey darkened as rain is,
alpha-blended before the grade (the night darkens them) and depth-read so the island stands in
front. Their strength follows the rain, or a third of the cloud cover under a heavy overcast.
A first build was too faint to see against a pale shower sky and floated above the horizon

## Loop pass 255 (2026-10-20) — the dawn chorus

At first light the birds sing most, but the soundscape treated dawn as any hour (and the night's

in a violet halo three times as wide, thicker and brighter the nearer the strike (400-4000 m),

The same stormy captures showed the hut's clearing white from the air: the puddles' sun glint

## Loop pass 249 (2026-10-20) — rain-wet trees

The rain wetted the ground (darker soil, puddles) but not the trees. The jungle shader now takes

both take a glossy sheen of the sun (a sharp highlight on the leaves, a broader one on the bark)
where the sun shadow map lets it through, fading as they dry. Under an overcast or showery sky
the sheen is slight (little sun), so a soaked forest mostly reads darker and deeper; when the
sun comes out on the wet leaves it glints. `jungle --weather showers` shows the darker, wetter
trunks and crowns; the dry `jungle` differs from before only within its own run-to-run noise
(two captures of one build differ in 0.4-0.5 % of the pixels by 20 levels, as they already did
before the live gust clock: a probe without it measured the same).

## Loop pass 246 (2026-10-20) — rainbows

`TimeOfDayRenderer::DrawRainbow` draws, on the sky at the moon's distance round the point
opposite the sun, the primary bow at 42 degrees (2.2 degrees across in seven bands, red outside
to violet inside, the edge bands softer) and a fainter secondary at 51 degrees with its colours

## Loop pass 242 (2026-10-20) — shooting stars

A small touch for the night sky. `shooting_stars::At` (core, header-only) gives, as a function

The `east` hill's soft pinkish-brown smears (the last of the handoff's hillside critique) are

## Loop pass 235 (2026-10-20) — morning mist

The last weather item. A core `MorningMistField` finds the low damp ground on a 14 m world

08:48, dispersed by a wind above the trade wind's 1.15-1.6 and by rain. `MistBankRenderer`

## Loop pass 234 (2026-10-20) — gust fronts that follow the weather

The gust fronts that lean the grass, the crowns, the fronds and the sea's ripples together
(Loop pass 5) ran on the fixed trade wind: one every 21.5 s at 6.5 m/s whatever the sky did.
`WindGust` now has a live clock the game advances each frame with the weather's wind: the
fronts travel at 6.5 m/s times wind^0.6 and come every 140 m / wind^0.8 (a thunderstorm's wind
of 2: 9.9 m/s every 80 m, a front about every eight seconds) and fill more of their width
(their across-wind floor rising from 0.45 to 0.70); the clock accumulates the distance the
fronts have travelled, so a change of wind slides them on instead of making them jump. The
shared shader function reads it from `uGustClock` (bound by the grass, jungle, palm, ocean and
terrain shaders) and the CPU form (`Strength`, used by the blown sand, the coconuts, the
leaves, the mists and the soundscape's gusts) from the same clock; unset (every test, and the
fixed form before the game's first frame) both keep the former trade-wind form. As before a
gust never raises a sway amplitude: it only makes the existing sway lean together, so every
collision and clearance envelope stays as authored. Core check: a storm's fronts come at least
twice as often, and a wind rising over 30 s never makes a front jump.

(0.31 and 0.83 cycles a metre) on flat ground (fading out between 0.10 and 0.17 rad) of the

a glance (a cool sky tone, lit with the ground's light, graded at night like everything) and
catching the sun as a sharp glint where the sun shadow map lets it through. `hut`, `jungle` and
`east` with `--weather showers` or `thunderstorm` (the forced weather starts soaked) show them;
dry weather changes nothing.

## Loop pass 209 (2026-10-20) — grass changes detail per patch, not per 37.5 m cell

A read-only audit of every camera-distance transition (after the operator's "everything
changes like stripes" in flight) ranked the grass mesh tiers first. The tier was chosen per
37.5 m cell by the cell centre's distance: a cell centred 70 m away put half its patches
on the middle mesh (10 proxy blades, no turf), the nearest of them 51 m from the camera,
inside full-size grass, so whole squares thinned together and adjacent cells at different
mixes met along straight cell edges, sweeping past in flight. Now every patch carries its
rank in its cell's hashed order as an instance attribute (the instance grew from 44 to 48
bytes), and the vertex shader gives each tier's mesh the patch's own share by the patch's
own distance: a patch of rank r leaves the near mesh at 78 - 16 r m and reaches the far
mesh at 102 - 16 r m, both meshes scaled over +-2.5 m, so no patch pops and nothing nearer
than 59.5 m leaves the near mesh. Each cell's instances are grouped by quarter, each quarter
in hashed order, and `GrassLod::Ranges` gives the contiguous instance range each tier must
draw for a quarter from its nearest and farthest anchors (clamped to the grass draw
distance). The BasicEffect fallback keeps the old split.

The core check covers every patch with weight in its tier's range (counts 1 to 333, cells
0 to 183 m), keeps the weights in 0..1 summing to 1, bounds the morph at 0.3 % per cm, and
contrasts the old split. The cost is vertex work: with the near mesh at 862 vertices, the
middle 60 and far 42, the estimated grass vertices per frame go from 1.23 M to 1.61 M
(`grass`), 0.84 M to 1.04 M (`hut`) and 0.62 M to 0.81 M (`ground`), and 32 to 47 instanced
draws instead of about 10; without the quarters they were 2.03 M, 1.16 M and 1.14 M. Native
`grass`, `hut` and `ground` pass; the near views are unchanged (0.45 % and 0.86 % of pixels
differ by 20 levels or more, the wind). Startup: "grass mesh tiers change per patch at its
own distance, morphing over 5 m, drawn by quarter-cell blocks instead of switching whole
cells by their centre", pinned. Still open from the audit: the jungle floor's six hard
radii between 30 and 70 m, the hard canopy and palm far culls, the canopy and palm near/far
swaps and the beach-detail ring at 52 m.

## Loop pass 208 (2026-10-20) — the supervisor fixture's load flake was a marker race

`IslandGpuQualificationSupervisorTests`, long recorded as load-sensitive (pass 204 and earlier
handoff entries), was reproduced: six copies at once failed 2 of 18 runs, each time in a
different case, with the supervisor returning 1 where 0 or 4 was expected. A return of 1 is
the workload's own exit status: the synthetic game polled for its child's pid marker with
`exists()` and then parsed it, but `Path.write_text` creates the file before it writes, so
under load the game read an empty file, failed `int('')` and exited 1. The same pattern sat in
three more fixture markers (the game's own start marker, the forked grandchild's marker and
the launcher pid file). Every one is now written to a `.part` file and renamed into place.
After the fix: 0 failures in 36 runs at six copies at once and 0 in 30 at ten at once, under a
machine load of 11 to 14. The supervisor itself is unchanged; no timeout was widened.

## Loop pass 207 (2026-10-20) — the large objects keep a shadow beyond the map

With the sun shadow map on, the wreck's, hut's and helicopter's projected mass shadows in the
contact batch were switched off outright, so beyond the map's far fade (pass 206) those
three cast no shadow at all; seen from the beach or from the air they floated. They now stay
on under the map and take, vertex by vertex, the share of the shadow the map has faded out
there (`1 - sun_shadow_fade::Strength`, the same function the core check sweeps), so a near
structure is shadowed once, by the map, and a far one by its projected patch, with no seam
or pop as the camera moves between. A patch wholly inside the map's full-strength region is
dropped from the batch. `SetStructureShadowsEnabled(false)` became `SetSunShadowMapActive(true)`;
the inventory reads "contact-batch mass shadows N (only where the sun shadow map's shadows
fade out)" and the startup line adds "beyond that the wreck, hut and helicopter keep their
projected mass shadows, cross-faded vertex by vertex with the map's", pinned. Native
`shipwreck-wide` now draws the wreck's patch (1, where the previous capture had 0); it is a
low-alpha patch and from that view falls mostly behind the hull, so the frame changes very
little. `hut` and `helicopter-approach` draw none (both structures inside the map). Pass.

## Loop pass 206 (2026-10-20) — the far end of the sun shadows moves with the camera

The operator flew through the island and saw the scene change "like stripes". Pass 7c039b7
removed the screen-space canopy shafts and texel-snapped the map; this pass removes the last
camera-quantised edge. The shadow map is a square in the sun's view, re-centred whenever the
camera leaves its 8 m cell, and the shadows faded on that square's own edge, so at each
re-centre the visible end of the tree shadows jumped 8 m: in flight, a band stepping over the
ground. The shadows now fade on a rounded square (the 4-norm) in the sun's view around the
viewer itself, 52 to 63 m out, and the map's edge keeps only a 2 % safety band. The viewer's
point is the camera's column at the light's fixed 12 m target height, transformed by the
current light matrix every frame, so it moves continuously. A static assert in the new
graphics-free `SunShadowFade.hpp` keeps the fade inside the map's full-strength square for
every viewer position in its cell (63 + 5.66 <= 72 - 2.88). A first version aimed the light at
the ground under the camera's cell; that moved the fade's centre at each re-centre again
(the core check caught it), so the target height stays fixed. The island rises only to 40 m,
so nothing within 40 m of the viewer is faded at any height.

The core check flies a viewer 2 cm per step along a 48 m line across 10 re-centres over a
grid of receivers at 0, 12, 26 and 40 m: the largest change of any receiver's shadow share
is 0.27 % per step, where the old square edge fade jumped 91 %; every receiver within 40 m
keeps full strength. Startup: "they fade out 52-63 m from the viewer in the sun's view, moving
with the camera rather than with the map's 8 m re-centring", pinned. Native `hut` and
`lookout` pass with near shadows unchanged (0.7 % and 1.1 % of pixels differ by 20 levels or
more from the previous captures, the moving grass and fronds).

## Fix pass (2026-10-20) — a flight crash, and the stripes in flight

Two operator reports from a native flight. **The crash** ("The data is not the correct size
for this VertexBuffer"): the blown-sand field (loop 122) holds up to 48 puffs and over a
beach in a gust it fills (a core check now measures the peak at 48 of 48), but it was drawn
by a `RootingDustRenderer` whose buffer held the dust default of 18, so 19 puffs within the
40 m draw range overflowed the upload. The renderer now takes a capacity (blown sand passes
`BlownSandField::Capacity`), and it, the mist renderer and the small-fauna batch all stop at
their buffer instead of overflowing (the batch drops trailing triangles with a one-time
warning). **The stripes**: the screen-space canopy sun shafts (9de4885) were locked to the
screen, not the world, and switched on and off with the light at the camera, so a flight
between crowns swept the whole view into flickering stripes; they are no longer drawn (a
startup line says so, pinned, and the tool fails if the old shafts line returns). The sun
shadow map is also steadied: its light matrix is snapped to whole texels so each 8 m
re-centre keeps one world-anchored texel grid (edges no longer crawl in flight), and the
receivers apply a receiver-plane depth bias from the screen-space derivatives so crowns,
fronds and banks sloped to the sun stop shadowing themselves in bands. Native `stream`,
`deer` and the suite pass.

`FlickingCount()`). In the renderer a thin dark-pink stem dips from the snout to the ground
ahead by the amount and forks at its tip. The skinks report line gains "a foraging skink
flicks its tongue at the ground ahead every few seconds, tasting its way" (pinned). Core
check: among the fully simulated skinks watched from ten metres a foraging skink flicks
fully at least twice in twenty seconds, each in again within half a second, and no basking
skink flicks. Native `skinks` passes, after a renderer fix the capture exposed: loop 159's
proboscis was emitted only while uncurled, which broke the butterfly mesh's fixed vertex
budget (a fatal "Butterfly near mesh does not match its fixed vertex budget") whenever a
feeding butterfly came near the camera; the two segments are now always emitted (collapsed
to the root when rolled), `MaximumVerticesPerButterfly` is 408 (384 plus the 24), and the
gecko and skink per-animal maxima gain headroom (2400, 1760) for their tongues. Native
`butterflies` re-passes.

## Loop pass 160 (2026-10-20) — a frog blinks

A resting frog's eyes never moved. `FrogState::blink` (0..1) now carries the blink:
`BlinkDelaySeconds` (1.5 s) into a rest and every `BlinkPeriodSeconds` (7 s, plus a little
per frog) after, the eyes are drawn down into the head for `BlinkSeconds` (0.25 s), closing
at 12/s and rising at 8/s (frogs blink by retracting the eyes); a hop or flight holds them
up, and the blinks are counted (`BlinkCount()`, `BlinkingCount()`). In the renderer each
eye, with its iris, pupil and glint, sinks 8 % of a unit into the head by the blink. The
frogs report line gains "a resting frog blinks, its eyes drawn down into its head for a
moment every seven seconds or so" (pinned). Core check: among the fully simulated frogs
watched from ten metres at least two blinks begin within half a minute, each closing fully
and up again within half a second, and no hopping frog blinks (the throttled tiers hold a
blink over their skipped frames, so the check is confined to the full tier). Native `frogs`
passes.

## Loop pass 159 (2026-10-20) — a butterfly uncurls its proboscis

A butterfly hovering at a blossom fed with nothing to feed through. `ButterflyState::proboscis`
(0..1) now carries it: settled into a nectar hover at its flower, the patch or fermenting
fruit (not travelling, slowed to `ProbeSettleSpeed` 0.16 m/s) the butterfly unrolls the
proboscis at `ProbeUnrollRate` (2.5/s) and rolls it up at `ProbeRollRate` (4/s) as it
leaves; the feeds are counted (`ProbeCount()`, `ProbingCount()`). In the near renderer a
fine dark two-segment tube curves from under the head down and forward by the uncurled
amount, hidden when rolled. The butterflies report line gains "a butterfly settled into its
hover at a blossom, the patch or fruit uncurls its proboscis to feed and rolls it up again
as it leaves" (pinned). Core check: within a minute a butterfly of the first habitat
settles into a nectar hover with the proboscis fully out, and none resting or fluttering
along has it out. Native `butterflies` passes.

## Loop pass 158 (2026-10-20) — a rodent grooms

A resting mouse or rat only sniffed. `RodentState::groom` (0..1) and `groomPhase` now carry
the groom: `GroomDelaySeconds` (0.8 s) into a rest in the open the rodent sits up and
washes its face with both forepaws for `GroomSeconds` (2 s), the strokes at
`GroomStrokeRate` (9 rad/s), rising at 3/s and down again at 4/s; a scurry, a hide or the
next forage ends it, and the bouts are counted (`GroomCount()`, `GroomingCount()`). In the
renderer the head rises 7.5 % of a unit and draws back over the haunches, and each forepaw
comes up to the face, stroking down and out with the phase; the hind legs stay planted. A
new report line "a resting mouse or rat sits up to groom, washing its face with both
forepaws for a couple of seconds" is pinned. Core check: a rodent watched from twelve
metres grooms to full on a rest with its strokes advancing and settles again, and no
hidden rodent grooms. Native `mice` passes.

## Loop pass 157 (2026-10-20) — the resident turns their head to the walker

The resident's head stayed square on their body however the walker stood. The
`ResidentState::lookYaw` (radians, left negative) now carries the look: a player within
`LookDistance` (14 m) and within `LookField` (1.35 rad) of straight ahead has the head turned
their way, up to `MaximumLookYaw` (1.0 rad) at `LookRate` (2.5 rad/s), and the head comes
back to the front once they leave that; a player round behind is not followed. The renderer
builds the whole head section (skull, hair and curls, ears, eyes and brows, nose, cheeks,
jaw and mouth) on a basis turned about the neck by the yaw, the body keeping its heading. A
new report line "the resident's head turns to the walker within fourteen metres ahead of
them, and back to the front once they leave that" is pinned. ResidentTests: a player six
metres off to the left turns the head that way within a second, one straight behind is not
followed, one to the right turns it back the other way, and the head is square again once
they have gone, the pose audit holding throughout. Native `resident` passes, after a
capture-tool fix: its resident arm-swing bound (0.56 m) predated loop 132's campfire crouch,
which reaches both hands 0.59 m forward at the tour's start where the capture begins; the
bound is now 1.0 m with the reason noted beside it.

## Loop pass 156 (2026-10-20) — a gecko licks its eye

A resting gecko did nothing with its lidless eyes. `GeckoState::eyeLick` (0..1) and
`lickSide` (+1 right, -1 left) now carry the lick: a second into each rest, and again every
`LickPeriodSeconds` (11 s, plus a little per gecko) of a long rest, the tongue comes out of
the snout and over one eye for `LickSeconds` (0.5 s), rising at 8/s and gone at 6/s, the
eyes taking turns lick by lick; the licks are counted (`LickCount()`, `LickingCount()`).
In the near renderer a pink tongue tube with a rounded tip curls from the snout up over the
licked eye by the lick amount. The geckos report line gains "a resting gecko licks an eye
clean with its tongue every ten seconds or so, the eyes taking turns" (pinned). Core check:
resting through the hunt cooldown the gecko licks at least twice in half a minute, each to
full and gone, both eyes. Native `geckos` passes.

## Loop pass 155 (2026-10-20) — a hermit crab feeds

A hermit crab paused on the sand merely stood. `HermitCrabState::feedAmount` (0..1) and
`feedPhase` now carry the feed: paused, out of its shell and standing still, the crab's
small claw picks at the sand and lifts to its mouth at `FeedPickRate` (4.5 rad/s), the
bouts counted (`FeedCount()`, `FeedingCount()`), rising at 3/s and dropping at 4/s when it
forages on or withdraws. In the near renderer the minor claw's wrist (and palm and fingers
with it) dips 3 cm to the sand on the first half of each cycle and lifts 2.8 cm up and
7.5 cm back toward the mouth on the second, the forearm following halfway; the big claw is
held as it was. The hermit crabs report line gains "one paused on the sand feeds, its small
claw picking at the sand and lifting to its mouth" (pinned). Core check: a crab watched
from twenty metres feeds to full on a pause with the rhythm advancing and stops to forage
again, and no withdrawn crab feeds. Native `hermit-crabs` passes.

## Loop pass 154 (2026-10-20) — a snake lifts its head to look

A ground snake lay flat whatever the walker did short of its retreat range.
`SnakeState::headLift` (0..1) now carries the lift: with the walker standing off between
`RetreatDistance` (8 m) and `LookDistance` (14 m) a fully or reduced-simulated ground snake
raises its head at 2.5/s and lowers it at 1.5/s once they are gone; within the retreat
range it keeps low to slip away, and dormant it lies flat. The renderer lifts the first
seven stations by up to `HeadLiftHeight` (0.16 m) on a quadratic falloff from the head, the
head rings, muzzle and tongue following. A new report line "a ground snake lifts its head
to look at the walker standing off within fourteen metres, and keeps it low to slip away
closer" is pinned. SnakePopulationTests: the walker at eleven metres has the head up within
two seconds; gone to forty metres it is flat within four; at five metres the snake slips
away low; tree snakes never lift. Native `snakes` passes.

## Loop pass 153 (2026-10-20) — a perched bird stretches a wing

A perched bird kept both wings folded through its stay. `BirdState::stretchAmount` (0..1)
and `stretchSide` (+1 right, -1 left) now carry the stretch: about every
`StretchPeriodSeconds` (17 s, plus a little per bird) a perched bird not feeding, preening
or newly landed opens one wing out and down from its fold for `StretchSeconds` (1.8 s), the
wings alternating; a departure or flush drops it with the preen. The stretches are counted
(`StretchCount()`, `StretchingCount()`). In the near renderer the stretched wing's perch
fold is reduced by 85 % and its lift lowered, so tip, elbow and trailing edge open out and
down while the other wing keeps its fold. A new report line "a perched bird stretches one
wing out and down for a second or two every seventeen seconds or so, between its preens"
is pinned. Core check: through its stay the seeded perched bird stretches a wing for a bout
of a second or two, never while preening. Native `bird-preen` passes.

## Loop pass 152 (2026-10-20) — the bear sniffs the air

The bear's head only dropped for a forage and rose again. `BearState::sniff` (0..1) now
carries the sniff: `SniffDelaySeconds` (0.6 s) into each stand (not foraging, lying or
walking) the bear lifts its head nose-up and sniffs the air for `SniffSeconds` (2.2 s),
again every `SniffPeriodSeconds` (9 s) of the stand, and facing the walker in its alert
range it holds the head up throughout; the sniffs are counted (`SniffCount()`,
`Sniffing()`). In the renderer the whole head section (skull, face, muzzle, nose, ears,
eyes and the near facial marks, not the tail) pitches nose-up about the head centre by up
to 0.30 rad. A new report line "the bear standing lifts its head to sniff the air for a
couple of seconds, and holds it up facing the walker in its alert range" is pinned.
BearMotionTests: left alone for two minutes the bear sniffs at least twice, to full and
settled; the walker at sixteen metres has the head up within three seconds and held up
while they stay. Native `bear` passes.

## Loop pass 151 (2026-10-20) — a deer twitches an ear

A deer's ears only swung together toward the walker. `DeerState::earTwitch` (0..1) and
`earSide` (-1 or 1) now carry the twitch: every `EarTwitchPeriodSeconds` (3.1 s, plus 0.7 s
per deer) a deer not bolting swings one ear back and out at a fly for `EarTwitchSeconds`
(0.35 s), rising at 10/s and settling at 8/s, the ears taking turns; a bolting deer holds
both forward. The twitches are counted (`EarTwitchCount()`, `TwitchingCount()`). In the

(the eyes stay). The deer report line gains "every few seconds a deer twitches one ear back
and out at a fly, the ears taking turns" (pinned). Core check: a deer watched from sixty
metres (fully simulated, not alerted) twitches an ear at least twice in fifteen seconds,
each to full and settled, on both sides. Native `deer` passes.

## Loop pass 150 (2026-10-20) — a goat flicks its tail

A goat's short tail stood still whatever it did. `GoatState::tailSwing` (-1..1) now carries
the flick: every `WagPeriodSeconds` (6.5 s, plus 0.9 s per goat, the first flicks staggered)
the tail swings side to side `WagBeats` (two) times over `WagSeconds` (0.7 s) under a sine
envelope and hangs still between; the flicks are counted (`WagCount()`, `WaggingCount()`).
`BuildGoatMesh` takes the swing as a fourth argument and carries it to the tail's tip (up to

flicks its short tail side to side, two beats and still again" (pinned). GoatHerdTests:
within twenty seconds every goat has flicked to both sides and hung still between, and the
mesh with the tail swung differs from the still mesh in tail vertices alone, the tip over a
decimetre aside. Native `goats` passes.

## Loop pass 149 (2026-10-20) — a boar shakes the mud off

A boar stepping out of its wallow walked off dripping. `BoarState::shake` (0..1) and
`shakePhase` now carry the shake: a boar leaving the mud with its coat still wet (mud above

where the boar stands (`BoarHerd::LastShake()`, `ShakeCount()`, `ShakingCount()`). New
`MudFleckField` flings a ring of eight flecks from the flanks at each new shake, sideways
and a little up, falling under gravity and gone within 0.8 s, drawn by the rooting-dust
renderer in soil brown. The boars report line gains "a boar stepping out of its wallow
stands and shakes, the mud flying from its flanks" (pinned). Core checks: within ten
minutes a boar leaving its wallow shakes to full with its beat advancing, standing still,
and each shake is noted where a muddy boar stands; the shake flings eight flecks that
reach a body's height and fall within the second. Native `boars` passes.

## Loop pass 148 (2026-10-20) — a swimming crocodile draws a wake

A crocodile swimming the estuary left the water unmarked. New `CrocodileWakeField` lays a
faint puff of foam at the snout of every crocodile under way at the surface (submerged past
0.6, speed above 0.15 m/s, not simulated dormant) every third of a second, each puff a
`DustPuff` on the water that spreads and thins to nothing within 2.5 s, fainter than the
shark's cut, drawn by the fin-wake renderer in foam white. A crocodile on the bank, lying

under way at the surface draws a faint wake of foam on the estuary behind its snout"

bank lays none; the wake is gone within two and a half seconds. Native `crocodiles` passes.

## Loop pass 147 (2026-10-20) — a roosting fruit bat fans its wings

A hanging fruit bat hung still, its wings folded, until it flew. `FruitBatState::fan`
(0..1) now carries the fan: every `FanPeriodSeconds` (16 s, plus 2 s per bat) a roosting

a 9 rad/s sine while fanning and settling to still after; the bouts are counted
(`FanCount()`, `FanningCount()`) and a bat in flight never fans. In the renderer the fan

beat. The bats report line gains "a hanging bat fans its half-opened wings for a few
seconds every quarter minute to cool" (pinned). FruitBatColonyTests: within forty seconds
a hanging bat fans to full with its wings beating and falls still again, and no flying bat
fans. Native `bat-roost` passes.

## Loop pass 146 (2026-10-20) — a dragonfly dips to the water

A patrolling dragonfly flew its wandering line at one height. `DragonflyState::dip`
(0..1) now carries the dip: a second into each `DipPeriodSeconds` (6.5 s, plus 0.7 s per

ground) and back, the descent at 4.5 m/s while dipping, and the touch at the bottom is

throws a fleck of spray at each new touch (a 5 cm `MistPuff` rising a hand's breadth and

a hand's breadth of the dip height and the touch is noted there; a dip throws a fleck of
spray that is gone within the second. Native `dragonflies` passes.

## Loop pass 145 (2026-10-20) — a turtle grazes the bottom

A foraging turtle hung low over the sand with its head level. `SeaTurtleState::graze`
(0..1) now carries the grazing bite: foraging within `GrazeHeight` (1.2 m) of the bottom
the head dips in a 0.9 s sine every `BiteSeconds` (2.4 s), followed at 4/s, and each bite
is noted at the beak, on the bottom, as `SeaTurtleGroup::Bite` (`LastBite()`,
`BiteCount()`); cruising or surfacing lets the head come up at 3/s. The near turtle's

(0.02, 0.39) by 0.55 rad × graze toward the bottom. New `TurtleGrazeField` raises a puff
of sand at each new bite (0.16 × scale, rising a little, swelling and settling within
1.8 s), drawn by the stingrays' sand renderer. The sea turtles report line gains "a turtle

(pinned). Core checks: within a minute a turtle foraging low over the bottom dips its head
in bites noted at its beak on the bottom; a bite raises a puff of sand that settles within
two seconds. Native `turtles` passes.

## Loop pass 144 (2026-10-20) — hoofbeats

A boar trotting off from the walker or the bear, and a deer bounding away, went in
silence. `BoarHerd::RetreatCount` / `LastRetreatIndex` and `DeerHerd::BoltCount` /
`LastBoltIndex` now count each trot or bolt once as it begins, naming the animal; the game
notes a hoofbeat voice at it through the soundscape: `GenerateHoofbeats` (two variants,
1.4 s: a drumming of dull thuds in fours — a short burst of low filtered noise over a
soft 58 or 85 Hz thump, the fourth beat stronger, fading as the animal gets its distance;
the deer's lighter and quicker at 7.2 beats a second to the boar's 5.4),
`WildlifeCallType::Hoofbeats`, `NoteHoofbeats(x, y, z, variant)` (pending a second, heard
within about twenty metres, a 1.45 s slot), effects created and reset with the other
one-shots, and the first-played line "first positional hoofbeats played". General report
line: "a boar trotting off or a deer bounding away drums its hoofbeats, an original run
of dull thuds in fours heard within twenty metres, the deer's lighter and quicker"
(pinned). Core checks: the hoofbeats PCM is deterministic, two variants, 1.4 s, silent at
the ends, low and in distinct beats; the walker at four metres sends the first boar
trotting off, counted once and named, and a deer bolting, counted with the deer. Native
`boars` passes.

## Loop pass 143 (2026-10-20) — the float rides the swell

The float of pass 142 sat fixed on the water and the rod never moved. `ResidentState::
floatBob` and `rodLift` now carry the line's life: while fishing a clock runs and the float
rises and falls with two slow sines (±4.5 cm and ±2 cm), and every `RodLiftPeriod` (12 s),
nine seconds in, the rod is lifted for 0.8 s to check the line (a sine pulse); both stop
with the fishing. The renderer takes the float's height from the bob and raises the rod's
angle and tightens the line's sag with the lift. A QA viewpoint `resident-fishing`
(`ResidentFishDetail`, `PreviewFishing()` each frame with the resident's update frozen)
frames the resident from ahead and to the right, rod out and line to the float; the
capture tool accepts it and requires the fishing camera line. General report line: "the
float rides the swell on its line, and every dozen seconds the resident lifts the rod to
check it" (pinned). Core checks extend the fishing test: through the rest of the jetty
pause the float rides the swell and the rod is lifted once; the preview holds the rod out.
Native `resident-fishing` passes.

## Loop pass 142 (2026-10-20) — the resident fishes from the jetty foot

At the jetty-foot call (pass 31) the resident stood looking out along the deck with empty
hands. `ResidentMotion::SetFishingSpot` (the game gives the jetty-foot landmark) makes a

and out at 2.5/s with the pause (`Fishing()` reports it), and `FitPose` carries the right
arm forward by 0.95 rad × fishing (the crouch's reach and the wave composed with it) and
refits on a change. The renderer draws a cane rod out of the right hand (1.75 m, drawn
out by the amount), a line in two segments sagging to a float 16 m ahead on the water
past the deck's end, and the float itself (a small red-and-cream ellipsoid). General
report line: "at the jetty foot the resident casts a line, the rod held out in the right
hand and the float riding the shallows past the deck's end, and takes it in to walk on"

spot the rod comes out at that pause with the right hand forward, and stays in at the
lookout's. Native `jetty` passes.

## Loop pass 141 (2026-10-20) — shadows on the seabed

The flying birds cast shadows on the ground (pass 59's bird shadows) but the swimming
animals cast none on the sand below them. New `SeabedShadowProjection` (header-only, the
birds' projection for ground under the sea): an animal's position carried along the fixed
sun down to the bottom, refined twice, valid 0.15–9 m over ground below sea level and for a

fish (0.16 × 0.06, scaled), stingray (0.95 × 1.25), sea turtle (0.62 × 0.50) and the
present shark (0.60 × 0.16, scale 2.8), darker and tighter close over the bottom (84 alpha

below them, projected along the fixed sun" (pinned). Core checks: a fish a metre over the
seabed casts a shadow down the sun's line onto ground under the sea; one on the bottom or
far above it casts none; ground above the sea takes none. Native `stingrays` passes.

## Loop pass 140 (2026-10-20) — a stalking gecko wags its tail

A gecko creeping on a fly (pass 82) moved with the same slow tail sway as at rest.
`GeckoState::tailWag` (0..1) and `tailWagPhase` now carry the stalking wag: while the
gecko stalks the wag rises at 3/s and the phase runs at `TailWagRate` (9 rad/s); the

(those stalking). The mesh adds the wag phase to each tail segment's sway and widens the

swaying wide and fast until the lunge" (pinned). Core checks extend the stalk test: the
stalking gecko wags at full amount with the population reporting it, a resting gecko holds
its tail still, and the wag stills within a second of the lunge. Native `geckos` passes.

## Loop pass 139 (2026-10-20) — a basking skink's push-ups

A skink basking in the sun lay flat and still. `SkinkState::pushUp` (0..1) now carries the
push-up display: a second and a half into a bask in the sun, and every eight seconds or so
after (1.3 s more per skink), a bout of three push-ups over 1.5 s (a sine from slack to the
full lift, followed at 8/s); getting up, foraging or fleeing ends it. `DisplayCount()`

second and a half into the bask and every eight seconds or so after" (pinned). Core
checks: over a sunny minute the skinks give at least one bout with three or more lifts to
the full raise, and no skink up and foraging ever lifts. Native `skinks` passes.

## Loop pass 138 (2026-10-20) — a calling frog's throat pulses

The frogs' calls (the soundscape's scheduler picks an audible frog) sounded from a still
body. `Soundscape::ActiveFrogCall()` now exposes the call last given with its animal
index; when the played-call count rises the game tells the population (`NoteCall(index)`,

and pulses under its chin through the call" (pinned). Core checks: a frog told it has
called swells its throat within a quarter second, pulses it above 0.9 and below 0.25
through the call, and lets it fall slack within a second after; an index off the end is
ignored. Native `frogs` passes.

## Loop pass 137 (2026-10-20) — a crab waves a claw

A beach crab paused in the open only opened and closed its claws. `CrabState` now carries a
claw-wave display (`waveAmount`, `waveSide`, `wavePhase`): half a second into a pause in

for a couple of seconds, a second into each pause and every nine seconds or so after"
(pinned). Core checks: the first crab, paused in the open, waves for a bout of one to four
seconds and no crab waves while it moves. Native `crabs` passes.

## Loop pass 136 (2026-10-20) — butterflies bask in the sun

A butterfly at rest held its wings closed whatever the light. `ButterflyMeadow` now reads
the cumulus clock (`SetCloudClock`, the gust-front clock the skinks use): at rest with the

the old 0.86, blended between, and the resting change is gentle (1.5/s) where flight's wing
