basks with its wings held open, pumping slowly, and closes them when a cloud's shadow
passes over" (pinned). Core checks: with the cumulus clock set to a sunny moment over the
first habitat a resting butterfly there opens its wings to bask, and set to a shaded
moment it closes them again. Native `butterflies` passes.

## Loop pass 135 (2026-10-20) — the shark's fin cuts a wake

Nine seconds in every forty-six the patrol rides just under the surface so the dorsal fin
cuts the water, and the water showed nothing of it. New `FinWakeField` (CPU): while the
shark is present, visible and riding above `CuttingDepth` (−1.05 m) a foam `DustPuff` is
laid at the fin (0.15 × scale behind the head, on the surface) every 0.2 s, up to the
rooting-dust capacity of eighteen (3.6 s of trail); a puff spreads on the water and thins
over 3 s without rising, so the wake reads as a fading white line behind the fin; the
shark cruising deep, hidden or away lays none. A fourth `RootingDustRenderer` draws the
puffs in foam white (236,244,248) after the blown sand. Startup report: the renderer's
"the shark's dorsal fin riding just under the surface cuts a foam wake that spreads and
fades on the water behind it within three seconds" (pinned). Core checks: a synthetic
shark riding at −0.85 m lays a puff every fifth of a second, on the surface behind the
fin; cruising deep it lays none and the foam is gone within three and a half seconds; the
real patrol's first seconds ride high enough to cut the water and lay a wake. Native
`shark` passes.

## Loop pass 134 (2026-10-20) — a leaping dolphin's splash

A dolphin's leap (pass 111 gave it to the seabirds) came down without a mark on the sea.
`DolphinPod::Splash` now records where a leap ends — at the transition out of `Leap` the
dolphin's position is the re-entry — counted once per leap (`SplashCount()`,
`LastSplash()`), its age running for `SplashSeconds` (2.6 s). The game gives the sea's one
foam ring to the most recent of the seabird's strike, the crocodile's entry and the
dolphin's re-entry (the ring's position and age fraction chosen by the youngest), and
notes a positional splash through the soundscape's existing splash voice at the re-entry.
The dolphins report line gains "a leap comes down in a splash, the sea's foam ring and the
positional splash where the dolphin re-enters" (pinned). Core checks extend the leap test:
every finished leap is noted as a splash; a splash lies within a leap's travel of where the
dolphin left the water and its ring is gone within three seconds. Native `dolphins`
passes.

## Loop pass 133 (2026-10-20) — a turning fish flashes silver

A school came round in its own flank colours. `FishState::flash` (0..1) now carries the
turning flash: each update the fish's bounded heading step is read as a turn rate (full at
1.1 rad/s), the flash rising at 12/s toward it and falling at 3/s, so a hard turn (parting
from the shark, a route reversal) lights the flank and the flash is gone within a third of
a second once the fish swims straight. `FishRenderer`'s near fish lerps every body colour
toward lit silver (228,234,238 under the water light) by 0.6 × flash × a flank weight that
leaves the back and belly their own tones. The fish report line gains "a fish rolling
through a turn flashes silver along its flanks, brightest parting from the shark"
(pinned). Core checks extend the shark-parting test: within half a second of the parting a
flank flashes above 0.5 and every flash stays in 0..1. Native `fish` passes (luminance
deviation 20.0).

## Loop pass 132 (2026-10-20) — the resident crouches to tend the fire

The resident's campfire pause built the fire up (pass 89) while they stood straight beside
it. `ResidentMotion::SetCrouch` (0..1, asked for by the game while `CampfireSite::Tending`
holds) and `CrouchAmount()` carry a squat: at a pause with the resident standing still the
crouch eases in at 1.0/s and out at 1.4/s the moment they move; `FitPose` drops the pelvis
by `CrouchDrop` (0.36 m) on the same planted feet (its floor lowered with it), the leg
solver bending the knees forward, and both hands come forward and down to the fire
(the arm's hang vector turned 1.15 rad × crouch toward the front, the wave still taking the
right arm up out of it); a changed crouch refits the pose on the same feet. A QA
viewpoint `resident-tending` (`ResidentTendDetail`, `PreviewCrouch()` each frame with the
resident's update frozen) frames the resident crouched, lower than `resident`; the
capture tool accepts it and requires the tending camera line. General report line: "at
the campfire the resident crouches to tend the fire, hands to the flames, and stands again
to walk on" (pinned). Core checks: asked for at the campfire pause the resident crouches
most of the way within a second and a half; the held crouch drops the pelvis a third of a
metre, keeps the feet planted, both legs reachable and the hands forward; asked off, the
resident stands within a second. Native `resident-tending` passes (luminance deviation
34.7).

## Loop pass 131 (2026-10-20) — the swash takes the wet sand's prints

Every print, bare or cloven, kept for the trail's four minutes whether it lay high on the
dry beach or on the wet strip the swash runs over. `Footprint::life` now carries each
print's own keep: `FootprintTrail::Update` takes a `wetSand` flag and lays the print with
`WetLifeSeconds` (45 s) on the wet strip and the usual 240 s elsewhere, the density fading
over that life. The game passes the flag from the terrain's wet-sand surface under the
walker, and for the deer and boars from the shallows' bed or wet sand under them. General
report line: "prints on the wet sand at the water's edge are taken back by the swash
within a minute, those higher up the beach over four" (pinned). Core checks: a walk from
the wet strip onto dry sand lays prints of both lives, and after seventy seconds the wet
sand's prints are gone while the dry sand's remain. Native `wet-sand` passes.

## Loop pass 130 (2026-10-20) — the bear lies down at rest

The bear, like the herds before passes 119 and 126, stood through every rest.
`BearState::lieAmount` (0..1) and the motion's `restSeconds_` / `lying_` carry a lie-down:
a rest two seconds in with no walker in the alert range settles the bear at 0.5/s (a heavy
animal) and lengthens the rest by 8 s; an alert or the next walk has it up at 1.5/s.
`LieCount()` and `Lying()` report it. `ContactPose` carries the lie: the body origin settles
0.42 m along its up axis, the gait bob fades, and each paw's sole is blended from where it
stood to a tucked spot (the fore paws 0.34 m back under the chest, the hind paws 0.36 m
forward under the belly), set on the rendered ground there with the ground's normal, and
the chain solved as a planted leg is — so the bones keep their lengths and the planted-paw
audits (sole on the terrain, no penetration, two-paw support) hold through the fold; the
planted-paw slide invariant in the bear test is exempted while the bear folds or rises. A
QA viewpoint `bear-lying` (`BearLyingDetail`, `PreviewLie()` each frame with the bear's
update frozen) frames the bear down at rest, lower and nearer than `bear`; the capture tool
accepts it and requires the lying camera line. General report line: "a rest two seconds
in, undisturbed, settles the bear onto folded legs for a longer lie, and the walker's
approach has it up within a second" (pinned). Bear motion checks: with nobody about the
bear lies down within five minutes, its body 0.3–0.5 m lower with every paw on the ground
and the bones unchanged, and the walker at fifteen metres has it up within a second.
Native `bear-lying` passes.

## Loop pass 129 (2026-10-20) — hoof dust

A boar trotting off, a deer bounding away or a goat sidestepping left the dry ground
undisturbed. New `HoofDustField` (CPU): the game hands it every boar, deer and goat each
frame as a `HoofDustRunner` (position, heading, speed, scale and whether the footstep
classifier reads dry sand or bare soil under it); a runner at 1.4 m/s or more on dry ground
releases a `DustPuff` every 0.16 s behind its hooves (0.45 m back, scaled, alternating a

breeze and in the fronts, swell and are gone within 0.9 s. The rooting-dust renderer draws

of eighteen). General report line: "a boar trotting off, a deer bounding or a goat
sidestepping on dry sand or bare soil kicks up puffs of earth behind its hooves, gone
within the second" (pinned). Core checks: a trotting runner on dry ground raises a puff
every few strides, low and behind the hooves; the dust is gone within the second once it
stops; a walking animal, or one on wet ground, raises none. Native `deer` passes.

## Loop pass 128 (2026-10-20) — a low mist over the seasonal wetland

The seasonal wetland was wet ground and reeds under the same clear air as the dry slopes.
New `WetlandMistField` (CPU, no GPU resources of its own): ten broad faint `MistPuff`s (3.0–

environment field's ellipse at (0, −140), radii 18 × 13 m), each hanging a hand's breadth
to a knee's height over the ground (0.12–0.55 m, with a slow bob), breathing in density

the gust fronts" (pinned) and "wetland mist: 10 low puffs over the seasonal wetland wrap
back in at its windward edge as the wind carries them out". Core checks: the mist starts
as ten faint low puffs inside the wetland; it drifts westward; over two minutes it wraps
back in, stays inside the wetland and breathes. Native `wetland` passes (luminance
deviation 46.0).

## Loop pass 127 (2026-10-20) — a monkey scratches

amount, the elbow hint of a reaching arm and the limb unweighted; the skinning takes it

scratches now and then, a forelimb up at its flank for a second and a half every fourteen
seconds or so" (pinned). Core checks: with the observer twelve metres off, within a
minute a monkey scratches for a bout of 0.8–3 s; no walking or climbing monkey ever
scratches; the preview holds the subject mid-scratch. Native `monkey-scratch` passes
(luminance deviation 50.1).

## Loop pass 124 (2026-10-20) — rodents bolt from a snake

## Loop pass 123 (2026-10-20) — birds mob a snake

A bird flushed by a snake's head at its perch (pass 91) simply left. It now mobs the

does not mob. The soundscape gains the alarm chatter: `GenerateBirdChatter` (two

quiet gaps), `WildlifeCallType::Chatter`, `NoteBirdChatter` (pending a second, heard

"a bird flushed by a snake mobs it, circling low over its head for eight seconds and
chattering the alarm, an original run of sharp chirps heard within twenty-five metres"
(pinned). Core checks extend the snake-flush test: the flushed bird begins mobbing; four
seconds on it is still circling within six metres of the snake and has chattered once or

The gust fronts leaned the palms, the grass and the hung fish, but the dry beaches lay

seconds" (pinned). Core checks: the field has at least twenty sources, every one on exposed

swing (speed is zero) follow as before. A QA viewpoint `deer-bedded` (`DeerBeddedDetail`,
`DeerHerd::PreviewBed(0)`) sets the antlered deer down for a still capture, framed a little
lower and closer than `deer`; the capture tool accepts it, requires the one-batch population
and the bedded camera line, and validates it with the scene profile. Report line: "a deer
that lies up in the shade beds down onto folded legs and is on its feet within half a
second of an alarm" (pinned). Core checks extend the shade-rest test: the deer beds down
within three seconds of its shade rest; the herd without a light field never beds; a walker
at three metres has the bedded deer up and bolting within half a second. Native
`deer-bedded` passes (luminance deviation 24.8; the deer lies with folded legs, head up);
native `deer` unchanged.

## Loop pass 115 (2026-10-20) — a deer rests in the shade

With the solid casters' shade in the receiver sample (pass 114) the deer's lighting read
the shade, but the deer themselves lay up wherever a rest phase caught them, in full sun as
often as not. `DeerHerd::SetLight(const CanopyLightField*)` gives the herd the light over
the ground (crowns, palm heads and now the snags', plants' and structures' shade): when a
rest transition comes on sunlit ground (receiver sample at 0.6 m above 0.72), `FindShade`
scans twelve bearings at five and ten metres for the shadiest valid spot inside the home's
inner margin (so the home pull does not override the walk) and, if one reads below 0.55,
the rest becomes a walk to it (`seekingShade`, 30 s budget, heading re-aimed every update);
within 0.8 m the deer lies up there for six to twelve seconds and `ShadeRestCount()`
rises. A retreat, an alert or any other change of behaviour drops the seek; with no light
field the deer rests where it is. The game passes the canopy light field at construction.
Herd-behaviour report line: "a deer whose rest comes on sunlit ground walks to the nearest
shade within ten metres and lies up there" (pinned). Core checks: with one dense crown whose
shadow lands five metres east of the third deer's home, the deer is seen seeking shade and
takes a rest under the crown within half an hour of simulated time; a herd without a light
field never seeks. Native `deer` passes (luminance deviation 34.4).

Also fixed in the native capture tool: the engine's asset logger shares the workload stream
with the startup report, and when the report's buffer flushed mid-line the logger's
`[INFO][APPLICATION]` lines landed inside a diagnostic ("… 14 bare footprint[INFO]… /
s lead along the sand …"), so a pin failed on a run that was otherwise sound (the deer
capture of 08:42 and 08:43). The tool now lifts such logger lines out of a split
`island-simulator:` line before the pins are checked.

## Loop pass 114 (2026-10-20) — animals lit by the sun's solid casters

The sun shadow map darkened the ground under a snag, a fern, a bush, the hut, the lookout
and the helicopter, but a goat or boar standing in that shadow was lit only by the porous
canopy light field (crowns and palm heads), so a body in a trunk's or a wall's shadow stayed
in full sun on dark ground. New `SunShadeField` (CPU, one-metre grid over ±300 m, no GPU
resources): the jungle's standing snags, understory and bushes are baked as the same discs
at body height the sunlit-subject selectors count (snag 3 m × 0.6 m, understory 2.2 m ×
1.5 m, bush 0.9 m × 1.1 m, scaled), each shadow rasterised down the fixed sun line onto the
terrain (`AddDisc` lands the disc's centre on the ground, refines once with the ground
there, then tests each cell's own sun line); the game adds the hut (floor + 1.6 m, 2.7 m),
the lookout platform and the helicopter fuselage as structure discs (shade 0.85). The field
is read only through `CanopyLightField::SampleReceiver` (`SetSunShade`, depth 0.65): the
animal renderers that tint by the receiver sample (goats, deer, boars, monkeys, bears,
snakes, spiders, the resident) now darken in those shadows, while `Sample` — the ground
classifier's input — is untouched, so turf and ground-cover placement do not move. Startup
report: "the animals' lighting reads the sun's solid casters: 2331 snag, understory, bush
and structure shadows darken a body standing in them by up to 65 percent; the ground keeps
its porous canopy reading" (pinned by the native capture tool) and the general line "a body
standing in a snag's, a plant's or a structure's sun shadow is lit as the ground there is".
Core checks: the field bakes the jungle's casters; a disc five metres up shades the ground
where its sun line lands and nothing twelve metres off; open sea and off-grid points carry
no shade; a receiver under the disc reads it through its own sun line; a 64-texel canopy
field with no crowns reads 1.0, 0.35 with the field set in the disc's shadow, 1.0 for the
ground sample and 1.0 again once cleared. Native `goats` (luminance deviation 56.7) and
`spiders-bright` (subject 5 now that the selector's receiver sample carries the shade;
17.5) pass.

## Loop pass 113 (2026-10-20) — a perched bird flushes from a passing animal

A perched bird flushed from the walker, a coconut's thud and a snake, but sat on while the
resident or a boar walked up under its perch. The perched flush now takes the ground
walkers the flock already receives (the herds, the bear, the resident): a body within the
flush distance (9 m) sends the bird off as the walker does, with the wing clap and the
feather of passes 106 and 107; `WalkerFlushCount()` counts the flushes that only a walker
caused. The startup report gains "a perched bird flushes from the resident or an animal
walking up under its perch as from the walker", pinned by the native capture tool. Core
checks: an animal twenty metres from the perch leaves the bird sitting; one walking up four
metres off flushes it. Native `birds` passes.

## Loop pass 112 (2026-10-20) — the resident's tour calls at the lookout

The lookout stood on the resident's island without the resident ever going near it. The
tour now takes a second landmark with a facing: the lookout's ramp foot, two metres beyond
the ramp's end, where the resident pauses and turns to look up the ramp at the platform
(the pause-facing rule the jetty foot uses, pass 31). The tour diagnostic now reads
"resident tour visits 2 landmark(s): the jetty foot and the lookout's ramp foot join the
campfire, path and clearing calls; … at the lookout's ramp foot the resident looks up the
ramp at the platform …", and the native capture tool pins both the count and the lookout
clause. Core checks: with the world's jetty and lookout placed, a resident route given both
landmarks takes both, and within half an hour the resident pauses at the lookout's ramp
foot looking up the ramp. Native `lookout` and `resident` pass.

## Loop pass 111 (2026-10-20) — the seabirds follow the dolphins

The pod's leaps and the seabirds' hunts were unconnected. The pod now notes where its last
leap began (`DolphinPod::LastLeap`), the game hands each new leap to the bird flock
(`BirdFlock::NoteDolphinLeap`), and for a second after it any seabird on its high route
within 160 m (`DolphinJoinDistance`) with a school in play has its hunt timer set to zero,
as a strike does within 120 m: the birds come in over the water the pod is working, the
way they follow dolphins at sea; `DolphinJoinCount()` counts the joins apart from the
strike joins. The startup report gains "a dolphin's leap brings the seabirds on their routes
within a hundred and sixty metres in to hunt the school of the moment", pinned by the
native capture tool. Core checks: the seabirds start on their routes; a leap near a fresh
school brings one in to hunt within two seconds; a leap with no school in play draws none;
the pod's leap is noted where it began. Native `dolphins` passes.

## Loop pass 110 (2026-10-20) — the crocodile hisses at the walker

A crocodile came alert on its bank at the walker in silence. Coming alert (the walker inside
24 m, the animal out of the water) it now hisses once per alert (`CrocodileGroup::LastHiss`,
placed at its jaws) and gapes for 1.6 s (`HissSeconds`, the jaw target held at 0.62);
`GenerateCrocodileHiss(variant)` is an original low open-jawed breath (1.2 s of heavily
filtered noise swelling and dying away; the second variant with a 23 Hz growl under it),
carried by `WildlifeCallType::Crocodile` through the shared wildlife slot (1.25 s), queued by
`Soundscape::NoteCrocodileHiss`, heard within about thirty metres and dropped if the slot
stays busy a second and a half. The startup report's crocodile line gains "one coming alert
on its bank hisses at the walker, an original low open-jawed breath heard within thirty
metres", pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: the walker forty metres off draws
no hiss; at twenty metres the crocodiles coming alert hiss at their jaws and gape, and no
hiss is given again while the walker stays; the hiss PCM is deterministic, two variants,
1.2 s, silent at both ends, loud in its middle and low in pitch. Native `crocodiles` passes.

## Loop pass 109 (2026-10-20) — stream leaves wash up on the strand

A leaf out of the mouth drifted the lagoon for seventy-five seconds and then simply
vanished, even where its drift carried it onto the sand. The drift field now keeps the
terrain: a leaf on the lagoon that drifts onto ground at or above the waterline washes up
(`beached`, counted by `BeachedCount()`): it lies on the sand two centimetres up for two
minutes (`BeachSeconds`), the leaf renderer drawing it there among the strandings, and then
a new leaf enters near the source as before. The stream's drift diagnostic gains "and one
that drifts onto rising sand washes up and lies on the strand", pinned by the native
capture tool. Core checks: run until a sea leaf meets the shore, the beached leaves lie at
sand height out of the water and are never afloat and beached at once; the earlier
afloat-in-the-banks rule treats a beached leaf like one at sea. Native `stream` passes.

## Loop pass 108 (2026-10-20) — a leaf that lands on the stream drifts away with it

A crown's leaf or a bird's feather that came down over the stream lay on the water as on
the floor. `StreamCourse::Locate(x,z,distance,lateral)` says whether a point lies on the
stream's water (the nearest station from the water mesh's first row to the mouth, within a
metre along and the half width across) and where; `StreamDriftField::Adopt(distance,
lateral,variant)` puts a leaf there in its own colour, in a free slot or in the place of
the leaf furthest along (longest at sea, else nearest the mouth), which was about to be
launched again anyway; the leaf field notes each landing (`LastLanding`: where, colour,
slot) and the game hands a landing on the water to the drift and removes the lying leaf.
`AdoptCount()` counts them. The startup report gains "a leaf or feather that comes down on
the stream is taken by the current and drifts away with it", pinned by the native capture
tool. Core checks: a point on a stream station is located at its distance in the middle of
the water and one fifty metres off is not; a leaf that landed joins the drift where it
landed in its own colour, the drift staying full, and goes on down the stream with the
current. Native `stream` passes.

## Loop pass 107 (2026-10-20) — a feather from a flushing bird

A bird's flush left nothing behind but its clap. `CanopyLeafFallField::Feather(x,y,z,seed)`
lets a pale feather go a quarter metre beside and fifteen centimetres below a flushing bird
(nothing from a bird on the floor): a `DriftingLeaf` of a fourth variant the stream's leaf
renderer draws pale (226,220,206), falling at its own 0.28 m/s (`FeatherFallSpeed`, about
half a leaf's pace, each leaf now keeping its own descent speed), carried downwind at six
tenths of a leaf's drift with a rock nearly twice as wide, and lying where it lands as a
leaf does. `FeatherCount()` counts them, and the game lets one go at every noted flush
beside the wing clap. The startup report gains "a flushing bird lets a pale feather go that
rocks down slower than a leaf and lies where it lands", pinned by the native capture tool.
Core checks: a flush lets one feather go beside the leaf; over two seconds it comes down at
about half the leaf's pace; a bird flushing off the floor lets none go. Native
`ground-doves` passes.

## Loop pass 106 (2026-10-20) — the wing clap of a flushing bird

A bird flushed from its perch or off the ground in silence. `GenerateWingClap(variant)` is
an original half-second whir (six quick beats of air: low filtered noise thumped at 11.5 Hz,
or 9 Hz for a larger pair of wings, with a brighter edge, dying away by 0.46 s), built into
two one-shot effects and carried by `WildlifeCallType::WingClap` through the shared wildlife
slot (0.55 s). The bird flock notes where its last flush happened (`LastFlush`,
`AnyFlushCount` over perched and ground flushes), and the game hands each one to
`Soundscape::NoteWingClap`, heard within about twenty metres and dropped if the slot stays
busy for half a second. The startup report gains "a bird flushing from a perch or the
ground claps its wings, an original half-second whir heard within twenty metres", pinned by
the native capture tool. Core checks: the flush of the perched bird is noted at the perch;
the clap PCM is deterministic, two variants, half a second and silent at both ends; it
beats at least four separate times and is gone by the end. Native `ground-doves` passes.

## Loop pass 105 (2026-10-20) — the resident whistles on the walk

The resident now has a voice: `GenerateResidentWhistle(variant)` is an original whistled
phrase (1.4 s of 22.05 kHz PCM: three soft sine notes with a slide up into each, a 5.5 Hz
vibrato and a trace of breath; the second variant a different tune), built into two
one-shot effects at startup and carried by `WildlifeCallType::Resident` through the shared
wildlife call slot (1.45 s). `Soundscape::NoteResidentWhistle(x,y,z)` queues it at the
resident's mouth, soft (0.32) and heard within about thirty metres, dropped if the slot
stays busy for two seconds; the game gives it every 28 s of walking (the clock held at six
seconds while they pause, so the next phrase comes soon after they set off). The startup
report gains "on the walk the resident whistles an original short phrase every half minute,
heard within thirty metres", pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: the whistle

passes.

## Loop pass 104 (2026-10-20) — the resident's footfalls

The resident walked the island without a sound while the player's own steps sounded on
every surface. `ResidentStepTracker` (in the soundscape model, testable without audio)
gives a footfall every 0.68 m of a walker's resolved travel, left and right in turn, the
stride reset by standing or an invalid position; the game drives it from the resident's
state (walking mode, speed over 0.1 m/s) and hands each footfall to
`Soundscape::NoteResidentStep` with the ground under the resident classified by
`FootstepGroundAt(x,z)`, the player's own classifier refactored to take any position
(planks on the decks, shallows, sand, rock, grass by turf density, else soil). The
soundscape plays the resident's step through the footstep voice whenever the player's own
step does not need it that frame, with the surface's own effect, at half volume fading
out over 3–24 m, pitched a little down; `PlayedResidentStepCount()` counts them, and the
six-source budget is untouched. The startup report gains "the resident's footfalls sound
on the ground under them, sand, soil, grass, rock, shallows or planks, heard within
twenty-four metres", pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: a walk of 3.4 m gives
five footfalls left and right in turn, standing resets the stride, and an invalid position
gives none. Native `resident` passes with its eight motion stages.

## Loop pass 103 (2026-10-20) — the deer sentinel snorts the alarm

The deer were the one herd with no voice: the sentinel lifted its head at the walker in

a short rough tail; the second variant doubled, the way a deer stamps it twice), built into

rule). The startup report gains "the deer sentinel coming alert at the walker snorts the
alarm, an original short nasal blast heard within fifty metres", pinned by the native
capture tool. Core checks: the snort PCM is deterministic, two distinct variants, a second
long and silent at both ends; its blast lies in the first half second, the doubled
variant's second blast after it, and the tail is gone by the end. Native `deer` passes.

## Loop pass 102 (2026-10-20) — the boars' alarm grunt at the bear

A boar the bear sent off (pass 68) trotted away in silence. The herd now notes which boar

five seconds is dropped; the ordinary boar call checks hold. Native `boars` passes.

The shark patrolled its offshore ring whatever broke the surface near it. `SharkPatrol::

## Loop pass 97 (2026-10-20) — the dolphins keep a berth from the shark

The pod cruised its routes through the shark's patrol as if it were not there. `DolphinPod::
SetThreat` takes the shark each frame (while present and visible): a dolphin within 28 m of
it (`BerthDistance`) leaves its route and heads straight away from the shark, a metre a
second faster, until it is clear, then takes up its route again; `BerthCount()` counts the
berths begun and `BerthingCount()` the dolphins keeping one. The startup report's dolphin
line gains "a dolphin within twenty-eight metres of the shark leaves its route to keep its
berth", pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: the shark sixty metres off leaves
the pod on its route; eight metres off, the first dolphin draws four metres and more away
within eight seconds; with the shark gone no dolphin keeps a berth. The pass-96 suite run
had the known load flake of the GPU qualification supervisor test, which passed alone.
Native `dolphins` passes.

## Loop pass 96 (2026-10-20) — the rays flee the shark

The stingrays fled the swimmer but let the shark pass over them. `StingrayGroup::SetThreat`
takes the shark each frame (while present and visible): a ray within 9 m of it
(`ThreatDistance`) is treated as it is with the swimmer inside the burst distance, the
flight heading away from the shark instead, so a gliding ray turns off and a settled one
bursts from the sand with its ring of puffs (`ThreatBurstCount`); the nearer of the swimmer
and the shark is the one fled. The startup report's stingray line gains "the shark passing
within nine metres turns them away and bursts a settled one from the sand", pinned by the
native capture tool. Core checks: the shark twenty metres from a settled ray leaves it
lying; six metres off it bursts the ray from the sand, which glides away from the shark.
Native `stingrays` passes.

## Loop pass 95 (2026-10-20) — the schools part around the shark

The shark's patrol passed through the shallow-water schools without a ripple in them.
`FishSchools::SetThreat(x,y,z,valid)` takes the shark each frame (while it is present and
visible); a fish within 7 m of it (`ThreatPartingDistance`, against the swimmer's 3 m) has

at 1.9 times its pace; `ThreatPartingCount()` is the number of fish parting this frame. The

parts. Native `fish` passes.

## Loop pass 94 (2026-10-20) — dragonflies perch with still wings

The dragonflies hovered, patrolled and darted without ever landing. `DragonflyBehavior::Perch`
ends one patrol in three: the dragonfly settles onto a stem's top at half a metre

tool. Core checks: a habitat dragonfly perches still with level wings at the perch height
within three minutes and is off again within twelve seconds; the long-session airborne
band and determinism checks hold. The pass-93 suite run had the known load flake of the
GPU qualification supervisor test, which passed alone. Native `dragonflies` passes.

## Loop pass 93 (2026-10-20) — the frog's splash scatters the pool fish

The pool fish scattered from the walker but not from the frog that leapt in among them.

The two frogs on the plunge pool's banks fled the walker along the bank like the stream

its bank at ground height within twenty seconds; a stream frog never dives. Native `frogs`

## Loop pass 91 (2026-10-20) — a snake at the perch flushes the bird

A tree snake could climb to a perch and the bird on it sat on. The bird flock now takes the

the coconut's thud do, counted by `SnakeFlushCount()` as well as the flush count. The
startup report gains "a snake's head come within three metres of a perched bird flushes it
as the walker does", pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: a snake on the ground
five metres below the perch leaves the bird sitting; its head up at the perch sends the
bird off at once. Native `tree-snakes` passes.

## Loop pass 90 (2026-10-20) — a monkey flees a snake with the alarm

The monkeys shared the stand with the ground and tree snakes without a glance. The troop

monkey (`SnakeAlarmDistance`) and within three metres of its height sends it off as the

run had the known load flake of the GPU qualification supervisor test, which passed alone.
Native `monkey-tree` passes.

## Loop pass 89 (2026-10-20) — the resident tends the fire

The resident's route pauses at the campfire's call each lap (about eight metres from the
pit) without the fire taking any notice. `CampfireSite::Tending(x,z,pausing)` is the rule:
the resident pausing within 9 m of the pit (`TendDistance`) is tending it; the game eases a
tend amount up at 0.6/s while they stay and down at 0.3/s once they walk on, and hands it
to the campfire renderer (`SetTending`), whose flame and plume vertex shader stretches the
tongues and the smoke up a third at full tend (`uTend`). The startup report gains "the
resident's pause at the campfire tends the fire, its tongues and plume standing a third
taller while they stay", pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: the rule holds for
a pause two metres off, not for a walk past, not for a pause twelve metres off, and not
for a non-finite position; and the resident's authored route brings a pause within tend
distance of the pit within twenty minutes. Native `campfire` passes with its four animation
stages.

## Loop pass 88 (2026-10-20) — the deer's tail flags and flicks

The deer's tail hung still in every mood. `DeerState::tailRaise` (0 hanging, 1 flagged up)
is driven by the herd: a bolting deer flags it up (the white underside shown, as a deer
running from a walker does) within a fraction of a second, a grazing, resting or drinking
deer flicks it half up for 0.45 s every four to eight seconds (the period per deer from its
home), and it hangs on the walk; it rises at 8/s and falls at 6/s. The deer renderer lofts
the tail along stations that swing up from the root with the raise (less back, more up
along the length). The startup report gains "a bolting deer flags its tail up, and a
grazing or resting deer flicks it every few seconds", pinned by the native capture tool.
Core checks: the third deer bolting from a walker three metres off has its tail flagged
within a second and a half; with the walker gone it comes down; and a grazing or resting
deer flicks it half up and lets it hang again. Native `deer` passes.

## Loop pass 85 (2026-10-20) — a coconut crab climbs a palm

The coconut crabs worked the nuts on the ground but never climbed, which is the thing a
coconut crab is known for. `CoconutCrabGroup::SetPalms` gives them the palms; every fourth
forage of a crab that finds no coconut (`ChooseTrunk`: the nearest living palm of scale 0.8
or more whose trunk stands inside its range) is a climb: the walk to the stand at the
trunk's foot (0.42 m from the axis), then `CoconutCrabBehavior::Climb`: up the trunk at
0.3 m/s to 2.8 m, a four-second pause, down at 0.35 m/s, and off to rest at the foot; a
threat does not call a crab down off a trunk. The state carries `climbAmount` (rising over
the first 0.6 m) and the trunk's axis, and the crab renderer blends the body's frame from
the ground's to one with forward up the trunk and up pointing away from the axis, so the
crab hangs on the bark head up with its underside to the trunk; the legs work at the climb's
rhythm. `ClimbCount()` and `ClimbingCount()` expose it. The startup report's coconut-crab
line gains "every fourth forage without one is a climb up a living palm trunk, a pause near
three metres up, and the way down", pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: with a
living palm two metres from a crab's home it climbs the trunk, body turned up it, within
five minutes, reaches the climbing height, and is back on the ground within forty seconds
of the top; the long-session grounding invariant now allows a climbing crab to be up to the
climbing height above its spot. Native `coconut-crabs` passes.

**`spiders-bright` resolved:** with the sun-line proxy widened to every layer the shadow
pass draws (crowns, palm heads, standing snags, the understory and the bushes, each a disc
at its body's height), the selector leaves spider 0 (two casters) and takes spider 2 on open
ground at (−9.2, 5.5, −97.7); the capture passes with luminance deviation 17.4 (gate 10,
mean 35 against 28 before). The `[!]` in the sweep note above is lifted.

## Loop pass 83 (2026-10-20) — skinks bask in the sun and leave a cloud's shade

The cumulus shadows drift over the land since pass 37, but the skinks basked on regardless.

`CloudShadow::Cover` over each skink's spot now shapes its day: a basking skink the cover
rises over 0.5 on gets up at once and forages (`ShadeRouseCount`), and a foraging skink
whose bout ends on ground with cover over 0.25 keeps foraging and looks again in a second
instead of lying down; it basks only in the sun (`SunBaskingCount`). The startup report's
skink line gains "a basking skink a cloud's shadow covers gets up and forages, and lies down
to bask only in the sun", pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: the cloud field

and foraging at once and it never lies down in the shade; with the sun back it basks within
half a minute. Native `skinks` passes.

### Capture sweep after the lighting passes (2026-10-20)

The `geckos` failure in pass 82 showed that detail viewpoints not captured since the sun
shadow map, cloud shade, sun shafts and sun flecks landed (10/19–10/20) can fail their
luminance gates. A sweep of the eleven stale detail viewpoints with the pass-83 build:
`skinks`, `rats`, `beetles`, `cicadas`, `bat-roost`, `snakes`, `snake-head`,
`campfire-wide`, `monkey-climb` and `wetland` pass; **`spiders-bright` fails** (luminance
deviation 8.1 against its close-natural-detail gate of 10; it passed with 12.8 on 10/14 and
13.9 on 10/17). The frame is the same spot and framing as on 10/17 with the whole floor
uniformly about 40 % darker. Facts gathered: the subject (spider 0) stands at
(−15.2, 4.9, −138.6), 97 m inland on a gentle slope, cloud cover 0 at the capture clock, all
1000 candidates report canopy transmission 1, and a crown/palm-on-the-sun-line proxy finds
no caster over 698 of them including the subject, yet the sun shadow map (838 casters)
leaves the spot in shade. Pulling the QA camera back and up made the deviation worse (7.6),
so the framing was restored. The bright-view selector now scores each candidate by canopy
transmission dimmed by the cumulus cover and by crowns or palm heads on its line to the sun
(printed as `transmission=` with `cover=` and `casters=`, the tool's argmax contract kept),
and the spider lighting proof prints "spider QA spot position=… shore-distance=… slope=…
cloud-cover=… sun-shadow-casters=…". The cause of the uniform shade is not yet pinned
down at that point; the resolution is in pass 84 (the proxy widened to the understory and
bushes picks a sunlit subject).

The geckos rested, scurried and hid beside the fly swarms without ever noticing them. The

a resting gecko with a fly hanging low (under 0.6 m) within 4.5 m on ground it accepts gets
two new behaviours: `Stalk`, the slow approach at 0.35 m/s with the heading held on the fly
(fourteen seconds at most, abandoned if the fly gets beyond one and a half ranges), and

cooldown. A threat interrupts a stalk as it does a rest. The lunge is noted (`LastLunge`,

metre of the snap dart for half a second as from the walker's hand (`LungeDartCount`). The
startup report's gecko line gains "a resting gecko with a fly hanging low within reach stalks
it and lunges, and the flies dart from the snap", pinned by the native capture tool. Core
checks: a gecko with a low fly 1.6 m off stalks it slowly and lunges from the last span
within a minute, rests after, and does not hunt again within the cooldown; a snap among a
swarm sends its flies darting.

## Loop pass 76 (2026-10-20) — the crowns shed leaves at a gust front

Leaves drifted on the stream and lay on the floor, but none ever fell. `CanopyLeafFallField`

wind clock: for crowns within 60 m of the viewer, the arrival of a gust front (the same
front-and-draw rule the palms use for their coconuts, chance 0.4 per crown per front) lets
a leaf go from six to nine metres up the crown; it descends at 0.55 m/s, is carried downwind
at 0.9 m/s, rocks side to side and turns at 2.4 rad/s, lands on the floor (or the water) and
lies there forty seconds before it is gone; 48 leaves at most, the longest-lying replaced
first; mostly brown and yellow, now and then a green one. The leaves are `DriftingLeaf`
records, so the stream's leaf renderer draws them with a second call made before the

"at a gust front the crowns let go leaves that spiral down through the shade, drift
downwind and lie on the floor a while", pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: a
front has a crown near the observer let go a leaf from up in the crown within four minutes;
it descends, drifts downwind and turns; it lands and lies; and it is gone after its rest.
Native `fruit` passes.

## Loop pass 73 (2026-10-20) — beach crabs bolt down their burrow

Each beach colony has had a visible burrow since the debris-anchoring pass, but no crab
ever used it: a frightened crab only scuttled away. Now `CrabBehavior::Hide` is the refuge:
when the walker or the resident comes within the scuttle distance and the colony's burrow
lies within 3.5 m roughly along the line of flight (or the crab is already at its mouth),

few seconds", pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: a crab within reach of its
burrow, frightened from the far side, is down the hole within six seconds (hidden, at the
centre, below the sand); with the beach clear it comes up within fifteen seconds; and it
leaves the mouth for its bouts within half a minute. The earlier walker-scatter checks still
pass. Native `crabs` passes (luminance deviation 38).

## Loop pass 72 (2026-10-20) — goats spar head to head

The goats grazed, walked, rested and drank, each in its own range, and never touched one
another. `GoatBehavior::Spar` is a bout between two goats: at a decision roll a goat other
than the sentinel picks its nearest free neighbour within 12 m (not drinking, retreating or
already sparring) and both enter the bout for 16 s. They walk toward each other at the
walking speed, stop inside `SparReach` (1.6 m) and face each other; on a shared clock they
take turns lowering the head (the grazing head-down pose, 1.5 s a turn, the lower index
first), which reads as the shove. The herd's separation rule lets sparring partners close to
`SparContact` (1.3 m between centres, nose to nose) while every other goat keeps the two
body clearances; a partner is remembered after the bout until the two have drawn apart to the
ordinary clearance, so the close stance can be left at a walk. The sentinel keeps its watch
and never spars; an alert or startle ends a bout, and a goat whose partner is called away
stands a moment and goes on. `SparringCount()`, `SparCount()` and `SparPartner(i)` expose it;
the soundscape gives a sparring goat the hoof-strike call. The startup report gains "goats
square up to a neighbour for a bout of head-to-head shoving, standing nose to nose and taking
turns lowering their heads", pinned by the native capture tool. Goat herd checks: two goats
stand nose to nose within eight minutes (the sentinel never among them), facing each other
inside the reach, and each lowers its head in turn while the other holds its head up; the
overlap rule exempts partners down to the contact distance; the behaviour bookkeeping array
grew to six entries (it had four for five behaviours). Native `goats` passes (luminance
deviation 57).

A seabird that had finished its low circling over a school climbed straight back to its

sea the light field reads as fully occluded, so the camera must be over land more than 5 m

## Loop pass 38 (2026-10-20) — spray at the cascade's foot

The drop of pass 6 had foam at the lip and nothing in the air. A core `CascadeMistField`
releases a puff of spray every 0.26 s where the drop meets the pool (the first station
below the lip, spread across 1.2 of the channel's half-width): each rises at 0.9 m/s scaled
by the drop (slowing through its 2.6 s life), drifts downstream at 0.28 m/s, is laid over
downwind at up to 0.9 m/s by a passing gust front (the field reads `WindGust` at the foot on
the coconuts' clock), swells from about 0.25 m to near a metre and thins, its density a
half-sine over its life. `CascadeMistRenderer` draws each puff as a camera-facing ten-segment
fan, pale spray fading to clear at the rim, alpha 58 at full density, premultiplied for the
alpha-blend state (the first capture showed solid white discs without that), with depth
read after the drifting leaves. Diagnostic "a mist of spray hangs at the cascade's foot,
rising and drifting on the breeze and laid over by the gust fronts" is pinned by the native
capture tool. Core checks: the cascade has a drop; over ten seconds the puffs rise more than
0.45 m above the pool while dense, never stray more than 6 m from the foot or 4 m up, and at
least six hang in the air at once (the first draft rose too slowly for its own threshold on
this drop's height, and the second scaled density by the 0.53 m drop to a peak of 0.5; a
drop now gives at least 0.6 of full density). Native `cascade` passes.

## Loop pass 37 (2026-10-20) — the cumulus shadows cross the land

Pass 5 put the cumulus shadows on the open sea and kept them off the lagoon so the sunlit
beach and the water beside it would not disagree; the land itself had none. The cloud field
(hash, value noise, drift with the trade wind, 0.56–0.70 threshold) now lives once in
`CloudShadow.hpp` as GLSL plus a CPU mirror, the ocean uses it without the lagoon gate, and
the sun shadow map's receiver snippet (`SunShadowMap::ReceiverShader`, now a string that
begins with the cloud field) multiplies `sunShadowVisibility()` by `1 − 0.38 · cover` on
every path, map or no map, so the terrain, grass, jungle and palms all dim together under a
cloud; `SunShadowMap::SetCloudClock` (the render clock, set every frame) feeds the new
`uCloudShade` uniform through both Bind paths. Diagnostic "the cumulus shadows drift over
the land as well as the sea, dimming every sun-shadow receiver together" is printed in the
startup report and pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks on the CPU mirror: the
shade covers between 8 % and 50 % of a 600 m square with soft edges, and the pattern 30 s
earlier matches the pattern displaced by 30 s of drift within 0.05. Native `shipwreck-wide`
and `beach` pass. (The first draft's ocean edit sliced to the vertex body's copy of the wind
exposure function and duplicated half the file; the fragment body's copy is the anchor.)

## Loop pass 36 (2026-10-20) — coconuts that strike the shallows float ashore

A nut shaken from a palm leaning over the water fell through the surface to the seabed and
lay there. The gust path's crown drop is now `FallingFruitField::ShakeCoconut` (public, so
the tests can shake one), which lands a nut over the shallows on the surface rather than the
bed; a coconut whose first strike is on ground below sea level counts no thud and goes
`afloat`: it rides half under the surface with a 3 cm bob, drifts downwind at 0.22 m/s with
a slow sideways set, and where the ground rises above the sea it beaches (`BeachedCount`)
and lies on the sand as any other nut, or is lost after eight minutes or 400 m. The fruit
diagnostic gains "a nut that strikes the shallows floats and drifts ashore", pinned by the
native capture tool. Core check: a nut shaken from a palm 2.5 m outside the east shore
floats at the surface over the shallows, drifts in and washes up on the sand within a
minute with no thud counted. Native `palms` passes.

## Loop pass 35 (2026-10-20) — the birds' shadows cross the ground

The flying birds cast nothing; the sun shadow map's casters are static. A core
`BirdShadowProjection` carries a bird's position down the fixed sun's rays to the ground
(two refinements for the ground's own height) and accepts it only between 0.3 and 40 m up
and over land. `BirdShadowRenderer` draws one terrain-conforming twelve-segment ellipse per
flying bird within 70 m (perched and ground-foraging birds excluded), along the heading with
the wings across it, spreading 6 % per metre of height, its centre alpha 96 scaled by a
height fade (full to 4 m, gone at 40 m) and a distance fade (40–70 m), alpha-blended with
depth read right after the contact shadows in the same pass. Diagnostic "flying birds cast
soft moving shadows on the ground below them, projected along the fixed sun" is pinned by
the native capture tool. Core checks on the east beach twenty metres inland: birds 6 and 18 m
up both cast; the shadow lies away from the sun and the higher bird's more than twice as far;
a bird on the ground and a bird over the sea cast none (the first draft's test point was 8 m
inside the shore, where the high bird's shadow fell on the water). Native `birds` passes.

## Loop pass 34 (2026-10-20) — the hut yard's hung fish and net swing

The split fish on the drying rack and the net on its frame hung rigid while the grass round
the hut leaned to every front. The hut mesh builder now tags the fish (40) and the net's
cords and rows (48) in the colour alpha the material shader already carries as its material
tag (both read as plain timber in the fragment shader, as 64 did), and records the bar and
rail heights in world y. The hut vertex shader takes `uGust` (the gust strength at the hut on
the render clock), `uSeconds` and `uHangTop`: a tagged vertex swings by how far it hangs
below its pivot (0.37 m for the fish, 0.9 m for the net), a light 1.2 cm sway in the breeze
plus up to 9 cm laid over downwind and a 3 cm sideways shiver in a gust front, with per-piece
phases from the vertex colour. `HutRenderer::Draw` takes the render seconds (the game passes
`timeSeconds`); the BasicEffect fallback ignores it. The yard diagnostic gains "the hung fish
and the net swing in the breeze and lay over in a gust front", pinned by the native capture
tool. Native `hut` passes; the effect is shader-only and has no CPU test beyond the pin.

## Loop pass 33 (2026-10-20) — turtle hatchlings scramble to the surf

The two turtle nests were disturbed sand with tracks and nothing ever came out of them. A
core `HatchlingField` takes the nest positions from the beach details (set after the
natural props are placed): on the first update (a software capture renders well under a
second of simulated time, so the nest capture shows them), and every 140 s after, a clutch
of twelve breaks
out of the next nest in turn, each hatchling placed on a small ring round the nest on its
own line a little off seaward, and scrambles at 0.18–0.26 m/s in bursts with a wobble about
the seaward heading (the outward radial), the heading pulled back to seaward as it goes; at
the first point where the ground is below sea level it is counted as reaching the surf,
swims straight out at 0.45 m/s on the surface for 14 s and is gone. `HatchlingRenderer`
draws each as a 5 cm domed shell over a paler rim with four paddling flippers, one dynamic
draw after the fruit. Diagnostic "turtle hatchlings break out of the nests in clutches and
scramble down the sand to the surf" is pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks on a
nest six metres inside the east shore: a full clutch is out within ten seconds; over three
minutes every scrambling hatchling stays on dry sand between the nest and the sea at ground
height, and at least three reach the surf. Native `turtle-nest` passes.

## Loop pass 32 (2026-10-20) — the fish rise to the drifting leaves

The pool fish and the drifting leaves shared the water without noticing each other. The fish
field now reads the leaf span each frame (`StreamFishField::SetLeaves`, set by the game from
the drift field): a holding fish with a leaf inside 1.2 m that has not yet passed it brings
its next dart forward at once and steers the dart's lateral line to the leaf's, so the fish
rises under the leaf and drifts back; `RiseCount()` counts these and the ordinary dart
clock resumes after. The fish diagnostic gains "a leaf drifting over a fish draws it up in a
dart", pinned by the native capture tool. Core check: with the drift field feeding the pool,
a fish rises to a leaf within five simulated minutes and every fish is still inside the
pool. Native `cascade` passes.

## Loop pass 31 (2026-10-20) — the resident looks out to sea at the jetty

The resident's call at the jetty foot was a pause facing wherever the path happened to point.
`ResidentRoute` takes one facing per landmark (`landmarkFacings`, unit x/z) and keeps a
`PauseFacings()` list parallel to its pause points (NaN for the authored pauses); the game
passes the jetty's seaward direction for the jetty-foot landmark. In `ResidentMotion::Step`
a pause that starts at a point with a facing lasts 8 s longer and, while it lasts, the
desired heading is that facing instead of the next route point, so the resident turns at the
usual 1.1 rad/s shuffle to stand looking out along the deck, then turns back onto the path;
`LookingOut()` reports it. The resident diagnostic gains "at the jetty foot the resident
turns to look out along the deck to sea", pinned by the native capture tool. Resident
checks: the facings pair with the pause points and the jetty pause carries one; walking the
tour at 20 Hz for up to fifty simulated minutes, the resident is found pausing within 5 m of
the jetty foot with its heading within 0.3 rad of seaward. Native `resident` passes.

## Loop pass 30 (2026-10-20) — small fish in the plunge pool

The cascade's pool held water and nothing else. A core `StreamFishField` keeps ten small fish
on its own course copy between the first station below the drop and the pool's last: each
has a holding station (course distance, lateral fraction, depth 6–22 cm under the surface,
`Place` resolving all three to a point above the bed), faces upstream with a slow sway, and
every 4–9 s darts 1.2 m upstream in 0.6 s before drifting back at 0.35 m/s. When the walker
comes within 4 m of the pool's reach all of them run for the deepest station (2.4 m/s),
crowd a little apart, sink deeper and hold there, flicking fast; left alone they rise and
spread back to their stations. `StreamFishRenderer` draws each as a 14 cm olive sliver with
a flicking forked tail in one dynamic draw before the stream water so the water tints them.
Diagnostic "small fish hold station in the plunge pool facing upstream, dart now and then
and scatter to the deep when the walker comes near" is pinned by the native capture tool.
Core checks: every fish starts and stays under the surface at its own spot inside the pool
(the first draft compared against the nearest station's level, which steps between the
pool's stations) and darts within a minute; the walker at the bank scatters all of them to
the deep within six seconds; thirty seconds alone spreads them back. Native `cascade` passes.

## Loop pass 29 (2026-10-20) — sand streamers in the gust front

The dry beach lay still while a front leaned the grass behind it and darkened the sea in
front. The terrain material now includes the shared `WindGust::Shader` and, before the wrack
line, lifts the exposed dry sand (more than 1.4 m inland, above 0.10 m, within 90 m) into
pale ribbons inside the gust band: a carrier racing downwind at 9 rad/s (toward −x with the
fronts) along a meandering phase, confined to a few lanes by a value-noise mask, brightening
the sand by up to 18 % at 55 % of the band strength. The fronts' clock is a new unwrapped
`uWindSeconds` uniform (the sea clock `uSeaSeconds` wraps at 628 s, which would have shifted
these fronts 24 m off the grass's after five minutes). Diagnostic "gust fronts drive pale
sand streamers racing along the dry beach" is printed with the terrain's report and pinned
by the native capture tool. Core check: the field peaks above 0.8 on both the east and west
beaches within three spacings. Native `beach` passes.

## Loop pass 28 (2026-10-20) — leaves drift down the stream

The stream's surface carried nothing, so its current was only implied by the shader. A new
core `StreamDriftField` keeps fourteen leaves on the course (its own `StreamCourse` copy):
each has a distance along the course and a lateral fraction of the channel half-width
(`Surface` resolves both to the water level between stations plus 2 cm, heading along the
reach), and `SpeedAt` gives the current: 0.32 m/s on the reach, ramping to 1.1 m/s over the
last 4 m above the cascade lip, 1.8 m/s through the drop, slackening to 0.12 m/s in the
plunge pool and back to the reach speed below it. Leaves wander across the channel and spin,
both faster in quick water; one that passes the last station is counted (`PassCount`) and a
new leaf enters near the source. `StreamDriftRenderer` draws each as a two-lobe pointed leaf
(green, brown or yellow) in one dynamic vertex-coloured draw right after the stream water,
outside the tracked scene draw count like the fruit. Diagnostic "leaves drift down the
stream on the current, hurry over the cascade lip, idle in the pool and go out to sea" is
pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: every leaf starts afloat inside the banks at
the water level; the current over the lip is more than three times the reach speed and the
pool slower than the reach; over ten simulated minutes the leaves stay afloat and at least
one reaches the sea. Native `cascade` passes.

## Portable evidence for loop passes 1–14 (2026-10-20, Web package of 2026-10-19 23:30)

Chrome software scopes against the Web package built after loop pass 14: `birds`, `boars`,
`monkeys`, `hut`, `grass-motion`, `butterflies`, `cliffs` passed in the first batch; `palms`
timed out there (overlapping a native test run) and passed alone at 00:35; `terrain` exceeded
its limit three times (600 s twice, 1200 s once at 00:56) with the machine's load average
between 16 and 21 from other agents, and a fourth time (1200 s, started 01:21 at load 7
that rose to 23 while it ran), and a fifth (1200 s, started 02:03 at load 7 that rose to
18), so it is `[!]` blocked by load, not by a defect: its evidence directories hold the
first captures each time. Retry `terrain` with `--timeout 1200` only when the load stays
under 8 for the whole run; the other agents' load has not allowed that tonight. Loop passes 15–27 are not yet in a Web package;
the next Web build and Android assemble cover them together.

## Loop pass 27 (2026-10-20) — cat's paws on the sea

The sea took no notice of the fronts that leaned every blade ashore. The ocean fragment
shader now includes the shared `WindGust::Shader` and, after the cumulus shadow, darkens the
water by 10 % plus a 7 % fine ripple texture (two crossed carriers at 7 rad/s) inside the
gust band, so a darker streak of cat's-paw ripples races downwind over lagoon and open sea
alike, in step with the grass, palms, plume and breeze swell. Diagnostic "passing gust fronts
darken the sea in racing bands of fine cat's-paw ripples" is printed with the ocean's report
and pinned by the native capture tool. Core check: the field peaks above 0.8 both over the
lagoon and 400 m offshore within three spacings (the across-wind envelope drifts slowly, so
one spacing can pass a point weakly; the first draft's one-spacing 0.9 rule failed on that).
Native `shipwreck-wide` passes.

## Loop pass 26 (2026-10-20) — the gust front lays the campfire plume over

The smoke drifted west on the trade wind at one fixed lean while the grass beside the fire
leaned to the passing fronts. The campfire vertex shader takes `uGust`, the gust strength at
the fire on the render clock (the same `timeSeconds` the grass fronts use), and the cool
upper plume's westward lean per unit altitude becomes `rise * (0.34 + 0.55 * gust)` with a
sideways tear of `0.30 * gust` on a 0.9 Hz carrier, so the column lies over and shreds as a
front passes and stands again behind it. The rule lives once in core as `CampfirePlume::Lean`
(the renderer header is not visible to the core-only campfire test, which is where the first
draft put it) and the shader applies the same constants. Diagnostic "a passing gust front
lays the campfire plume over further downwind and tears it sideways" is printed by the
renderer and pinned by the native capture tool. Campfire checks: a full-strength front more
than doubles the lean, and the fronts do pass the fire (strength above 0.9 within one front
spacing). Native `campfire` passes.

## Loop pass 25 (2026-10-20) — the fruit doves land beside the fallen fruit

The fruit doves' ground visits went to a pseudo-random dry spot on their ring; the fruit the
monkeys knocked down (and the resident of the name) never met. The flock reads the fruit span
(`BirdFlock::SetLyingFruit`) and a dove's ground visit (every other perch cycle) first looks
for the nearest resting, non-rolling, non-coconut fruit on dove-grade ground (dry, above
0.8 m, more than 22 m inland, slope under 0.30 rad) and lands 0.4 m short of it
(`FindFruitLanding`); the existing forage walk then works the 2.4 m around the fruit. The
range is the whole island (240 m): a probe showed the doves' route decisions fall 180 m or
more from the test tree, so a 60 m rule never fired in six minutes. The visit counts in
`FruitLandingCount()`. The dove diagnostic gains "a dove's ground visit crosses to the nearest
fruit lying on dove-grade ground when there is any", pinned by the native capture tool. Core
check: with fruit shaken down on dove-grade ground near the first dove's start, a dove is
foraging within 3 m of a fruit inside six simulated minutes. Native `ground-doves` passes.

## Loop pass 24 (2026-10-20) — the fallen fruit bounces and rolls

A fruit stopped dead on the spot it struck, as nothing dropped onto a slope does. `FallingFruit`
carries a horizontal velocity and a `rolling` flag. The first strike (the bounce of pass 12,
the thud of pass 15) now kicks the fruit along the ground: 2.4 times the slope gradient downhill
plus a small deterministic sideways component, scaled by 0.12 of the strike speed; the bounce
flies on that kick, re-sampling the ground as it goes. When it settles it rolls: pulled by a
quarter of gravity along the slope, slowed by a 2.2/s drag and a 0.4 m/s² rolling resistance
(which beats the pull on gentle ground), and cut off after 3 s on a steep bank; the roll stops
below 0.05 m/s and `LastRollDistance()` records the distance from the strike. Monkeys, boars
and butterflies ignore fruit still rolling. Diagnostic "a fallen fruit bounces off where it
strikes and rolls downhill to rest" is pinned by the native capture tool. Core checks: under
the sloping test tree the last fruit to rest rolled between 0.08 and 4 m from its strike, and
resting fruit has no velocity. The first draft's drag-only roll never stopped on a sustained
slope (and starved the boar test of resting fruit); the resistance term fixed both. Native
`fruit` passes.

## Loop pass 23 (2026-10-20) — the gust front is heard

The gust fronts of pass 9 leaned the grass, thrashed the palms and shook coconuts down, and
the breeze bed played on unchanged. `SoundscapeModel::Update` takes a gust strength (0..1,
default 0): the breeze bed target rises by up to 90 % and the canopy (jungle) bed by up to
45 %, each under a ceiling (0.40 and 0.20), through the same 1.8 s blend as the zone mix, so
the swell builds and dies with the front's 20-odd second passage. `Soundscape` samples
`WindGust::Strength` at the listener on the clock the coconuts use (`SetWindClock`, set from
the game's sea-forage seconds every frame, the same clock the shaders' uTime fronts follow)
and passes it in. Diagnostic "passing gust fronts swell the breeze and canopy beds at the
listener" is printed in the game's startup report (the soundscape does not start under the
software capture, so its own report is not where pins can live) and pinned by the native
capture tool. Core checks: with a front held at full strength the beds settle above 1.5× and
1.2× the calm mix within their ceilings; with it gone they return within 0.002 of calm.
Native `palms` passes; the audio inventory is unchanged.

## Loop pass 22 (2026-10-20) — the resident's walk scatters the crabs

The beach crabs scuttled only from the player; the resident's tour along the beach (pass 13's
footprints run right through the colonies) walked among them untouched. `CrabColony::SetWalker`
takes a second walker, set every frame from the resident's position, and each crab now
scatters from whichever of the observer and the walker is nearer within the same 5.2 m
(`ScuttleDistance`), away from that one. Activation tiers stay observer-relative, so the
resident's walk animates crabs the player can see and costs nothing elsewhere. The crab
diagnostic gains "the resident's walk along the beach scatters them as the player's does",
pinned by the native capture tool. Core check: with the observer 40 m off and the walker one
metre beside the first crab it scuttles away from the walker within 1.5 s; with the walker
withdrawn it returns to its bouts within ten seconds. Native `crabs` passes.

## Loop pass 21 (2026-10-20) — the butterflies come down to the fermenting fruit

The clearing butterflies alternated the ground patch and the flowering bushes; the fruit
rotting under the crowns a few metres off was nothing to them. The meadow now reads the fruit
span (`ButterflyMeadow::SetLyingFruit`) and every other ground-patch nectar decision (the
nectar decisions fall on even transition counts, so the rule is count % 4 == 0; the % 4 == 3
first draft never fired) looks for the nearest non-coconut fruit that has lain 20 s or more
within the habitat's excursion reach on inland, gentle ground (`FindFermentingFruit`; the
clearing-surface rule is not applied because the fruit lies on forest floor). The visit uses
the bush excursion machinery, with the hover 0.22 m over the fruit instead of blossom height,
and counts in `FruitVisitCount()`. The butterfly diagnostic gains "fruit that has lain
fermenting for 20 s draws them down to feed low over it", pinned by the native capture tool.
Core check: fruit shaken down eight metres from the first habitat is visited within six
minutes, the butterfly hovering within 1.5 m of a target at the fruit height (the fruit
itself may have rotted away by then, so the hover is the evidence). Native `butterflies`
passes.

## Loop pass 20 (2026-10-20) — perched birds flush

A bird on a perch sat out its eight to fourteen seconds whatever happened beside it: the walker
could stand under the mooring post and the bird stayed. Now a perched bird flushes the frame
the observer comes within 9 m horizontally, and `BirdFlock::NoteDisturbance` (set by the game
from the coconut landing, alongside the herds') flushes every perched bird within 30 m during
the following second. A flush is the ordinary departure from the start (`Depart`, the 1.1 s
unfold and the 3.2 s climb to the route) and counts in `FlushCount()`; the bird then waits its
usual minute before the next perch. The perch diagnostic gains "a perched bird flushes when
the walker comes within 9 m or a coconut thuds within 30 m", pinned by the native capture
tool. Core checks on a flock seeded onto one wreck perch: a walker 25 m off and a thud 45 m off
leave it sitting; a walker 6 m off flushes it and it is flying higher than the perch within four
seconds; a thud 12 m off flushes it with no walker about. Native `birds` passes.

## Loop pass 19 (2026-10-20) — the thud startles the herds

The coconut's thud of pass 15 reached the player's ears and nothing else. Both herds now take a
disturbance point (`DeerHerd::NoteDisturbance`, `GoatHerd::NoteDisturbance`), which the game
sets from the landing the moment it notes the thud. For six seconds any deer or goat within
30 m of the point that is not already alarmed by the player stops, stands (the Rest pose) and
turns to face the fall at its ordinary alert turn rate, the goats shuffling round as they do
for a watcher; when the startle fades the grazing and wandering go on. The herd-behaviour
diagnostic gains "a coconut's thud startles the deer and goats within 30 m, who stand facing
the fall for 6 s", pinned by the native capture tool. Core and goat-herd checks: a thud twelve
metres from a grazing deer or goat (observer 60 m off for the deer, so it is fully simulated)
puts it in Rest facing within 0.35 rad of the fall inside the window, and the startle has
faded four seconds later. Native `deer` and `goats` pass.

## Loop pass 18 (2026-10-20) — the boars take the fallen fruit and coconuts

The boars rooted at trunk bases while fruit and coconuts lay about them. The herd now reads the
same fruit span the monkeys do (`BoarHerd::SetLyingFruit`) and a forage decision first looks for
the nearest resting fruit of any kind, coconuts included, within 0.9 of the home radius on valid
ground (`ChooseFruitTarget`); the fruit itself becomes the rooting site with the "trunk" one
metre beyond it along the approach, so the boar walks up and drops its nose on the fruit. The
first rooting frame there eats it: the index goes to `EatenFruit()`, the game consumes it from
the field, and the rooting pose carries on over the spot for the rest of the forage. Only when
nothing lies in range does the boar root at a trunk as before. Diagnostic "boars forage for the
fallen fruit and coconuts before the trunk bases and eat them where they lie" is pinned by the
native capture tool. Core check: fruit shaken down beside the first boar's home is eaten within
twenty simulated minutes with the observer 40 m off. Native `boars` passes.

## Loop pass 17 (2026-10-20) — the monkeys eat the fallen fruit

Pass 12's fruit lay under the crowns until its field slot expired; nothing in the forest cared
that it was there. The troop now reads the field's fruit each frame (`MonkeyTroop::SetLyingFruit`,
a span, no copy) and on every other wander decision that does not go to a tree it looks for the
nearest resting non-coconut fruit within the monkey's 34 m home range on valid ground and walks

under the crowns and eat it, idling over the spot" is pinned by the native capture tool. Core
checks: consuming a lying fruit counts once; a troop with fruit shaken down beside its first
member's home eats one within twenty simulated minutes (the fruit field advances alongside so
the fruit's rest clock runs). Native `monkey-tree` passes. Coconuts are left alone; the next
pass could let the boars take those.

## Loop pass 16 (2026-10-20) — the crabs work the wrack line

The wrack line of pass 4 was a shader-only band wandered by the terrain's noise fields, so
nothing on the CPU could find it. `WrackLine` is now one function in both forms (inland 5.4 m
plus two sines of the coast angle, ±3.1 m) used by the terrain material for the band's centre

feed. The crab diagnostic gains "every other bout works the wrack line and feeds among the
strandings", pinned by the native capture tool. New core checks: the line wanders a bounded
distance about its base and differs around the coast, and over four simulated minutes more than
an eighth of crab-time is spent within a metre of it. Native `crabs` and `wet-sand` pass.

## Loop pass 15 (2026-10-20) — the coconut's thud

A coconut's first strike on the ground (`FallingFruitField::LastCoconutLanding`, counted so each
landing is noted once) is now heard: `GenerateCoconutThud` synthesises a 0.45 s dull hollow
knock (a damped 96 Hz tone with a weak 215 Hz partial) and a short hiss of sand, the game notes

`WildlifeCallType::Thud` within a second when free at 0.40 falling to nothing between 4 and
32 m, holding the slot half a second; a thud out of earshot or too late is dropped. The clip

capture tool, and the grove core check also asserts the landing is counted where the nut struck
the ground. `IslandAudioPreviewExport` and native `palms` pass. Human listening remains an
operator check.

## Loop pass 14 (2026-10-20) — gusts shake coconuts from the palms

The gust fronts of pass 5, the coconut palms and the fallen coconuts of item 17 now meet.
`FallingFruitField::UpdateCoconuts` watches every living fruiting palm (forms 1 and 3) within
80 m of the observer: when a gust front arrives over it (the shared `WindGust::Strength`
crossing 0.85), a deterministic per-palm, per-front draw drops a nut one time in ten. The nut
starts under the crown (the mesh's frond base at 9.4 m plus the form's step, scaled, leaned

within four simulated minutes. Native `palms` passes. A thud for the landing is a candidate for
a later pass.

## Loop pass 13 (2026-10-20) — the resident's footprints on the beach

The animal track lines of backlog item 10 never showed a human. `JettyPlacement::FootprintLines`
lays fourteen bare-foot prints along the beach from the ramp foot past the canoe: the ground
straight up from this root rises onto rock within a few metres and the shoreline curves, so
the prints follow the actual shore arc on the canoe's side (a stride every 0.62 m, 1.4 m
inside the shoreline, feet alternating 0.11 m either side of the line and toed out 0.12 rad).
Each print is its own `AnimalTrackPlacement` (new track variant 2: heel, arch, ball and five
toes on a pressed rim) on the rendered terrain's height: a first draft placed three multi-stride
lines on the analytic height and all but one print vanished under the drawn mesh, since the
analytic field and the rendered surface differ by more than a print's thickness on a curved
beach. `NaturalPropRenderer` takes extra tracks from later layouts and draws them in the same
batches as the layout's own; the startup log adds "14 bare footprints lead along the sand from
the jetty foot past the canoe", pinned by the native capture tool. The `jetty` QA camera now
stands at the far end of the prints looking back along them past the canoe to the deck. New
core check: the prints lie 0.4–4 m inside the shoreline above the water, each stride further
from the root than the last. Inspected native `20261019T232710Z-jetty` shows the line of prints
from the canoe along the beach; `tracks` passes.

## Loop pass 12 (2026-10-20) — the resident calls at the jetty

The resident's closed tour (campfire, the path at z = 135, the west clearing, the path at
z = -165 and z = -100) never went near the new landing. `ResidentRoute` now takes landmarks:
extra tour goals inserted after the west clearing, each snapped to the nearest safe grid node
and joined by the same A* over safe segments, with its own pause point; if a landmark cannot
be reached safely the route is rebuilt without it rather than breaking the tour. The game
hands over the jetty foot, three metres up the sand from the deck's root, and on this island
the search reaches it (`LandmarkCount()` is 1), so the resident now walks down to the jetty,
pauses there and carries on. The startup log adds "resident tour visits 1 landmark(s): the
jetty foot joins the campfire, path and clearing calls", pinned by the native capture tool.
The resident tests and native `resident` pass.

## Loop pass 11 (2026-10-20) — the water at the jetty posts, and a perch on the lookout

Two small truths the new structures lacked. The ocean shader now takes the jetty's root and
direction (`uJettyLine`) and reconstructs the post positions in deck coordinates (pairs every
2.8 m from 1.6 m, 0.72 m either side, the mooring post at 13.5 m): each post standing in water
wears a foam collar that breathes with the swell and trails a short foam streak downwind of
it, through the existing foam term. The lookout's back-left rail post top is a ninth
structure perch (`LookoutPlacement::RailPerch`, added before the flock's perch list is set, so
the birds use it). Both structure diagnostics gain their new clause ("the water collars its
posts with foam"; "a rail-post perch for the birds"), re-pinned by the native capture tool, and
the lookout core check also asserts the perch sits above the platform. Inspected native
`20261019T230913Z-jetty` shows pale collars at the posts in the shallows; `lookout` and `birds`
pass.

## Loop pass 10 (2026-10-20) — fruit knocked loose by picking monkeys

The fruiting crowns, the monkeys' preference for them and the static fallen coconuts never met:
nothing ever fell. `FallingFruitField` watches the troop; while a monkey is `InspectTree` on a
fruiting crown (`pickingFruit`) and not dormant, every 4.5 s (the first soon after picking
starts) a fruit drops from one of that tree's four fruiting lobes, placed like the crown
geometry (the lobe's outer underside, then the instance scale, yaw and translation), falls
under gravity, bounces once lightly if it strikes hard, and lies on the ground for 90 s before
it is gone; the field holds 24 and recycles the longest-lying. `FallingFruitRenderer` rebuilds
small faceted spheres (orange for form 2, purple for form 5, darkening a little as they age)
into one dynamic vertex-coloured draw within 90 m. The startup log adds "fruit knocked loose
by picking monkeys drops from the crown and lies under the tree", pinned by the native capture
tool. New core check with a synthetic picking monkey: several fruit drop within half a minute,
start up in the crown and land on the ground under the tree. Native `monkey-tree` and `fruit`
pass. In this pass's full run `IslandGpuQualificationSupervisorTests` failed once under
`ctest -j 3` (`test_failed_workload_is_not_qualified` saw exit 1 instead of 7) and passed when
run alone; it exercises the supervisor's lock and process handling, so it is load-sensitive
rather than related to the fruit.
