## Loop pass 9 (2026-10-20) — the strike's splash

The plunge of pass 7 was silent. `GenerateBirdSplash` synthesises a 0.7 s strike (a hard
attack, a spray of droplets peaking at 0.16 s, the water closing over it), the game notes every
new `DiveCount` to the soundscape (`NoteBirdSplash` at the strike point on the water surface),
and the wildlife one-shot slot plays it as `WildlifeCallType::Splash` within 1.5 s when free,
at 0.36 falling to nothing between 12 and 82 m, holding the slot 0.75 s; a strike that cannot
play in time or is out of earshot is dropped rather than queued. The clip joins the audio
inventory (56 clips, 7,278,700 PCM bytes pinned). The plunge diagnostic now ends "and a
positional splash", pinned by the native capture tool; `IslandAudioPreviewExport` and the core
checks pass, and native `birds` passes. Human listening remains an operator check.

## Loop pass 8 (2026-10-20) — the resident's lookout tower

The second half of backlog item 14: a walkable lookout. A tree platform would need climbing
through the trunk's own collision proxy, so the lookout is a post tower in the hut clearing:
`LookoutLayout::FindInWorld` fans eighteen bearings round the hut's left side and back at 8.4 m
and takes the first whose platform square and ramp run lie on ground with less than 0.9 m
relief (the rendered surface's height range), above the 30 m shore distance, clear of every
world obstacle by 1.2 m, with a ramp no steeper than 0.47 rad. Four posts sunk 0.45 m carry a
2.5 m plank platform 3.2 m above the highest post ground with two-bar rails on three sides, and
a 7.6 m cleated ramp runs from the open side down to the ground away from the hut.
`LookoutPlacement::SupportHeight` lifts the walker on the platform and along the ramp
(`PlayerMotion::SetLookout`, after the other structure supports), the four posts join the world
obstacles, and the decks ring wooden underfoot. `LookoutRenderer` (784 triangles, one
vertex-coloured draw on the shared builder, sun-shadow caster) draws posts, braces, planks,
rails, stringers, planks and cleats. A `lookout` QA viewpoint stands beside the ramp foot
looking up it. The startup log adds "resident's lookout tower beside the hut carries a railed
platform the walker climbs by a cleated ramp", pinned by the native capture tool. New core
checks: a site exists beside the authored hut clearing, the platform stands three metres up, the
ramp carries the walker between the ground and the platform, its slope is within the walk limit,
and the support leaves the ground beside it alone. Inspected native `20261019T225658Z-lookout`
shows the ramp, posts and railed platform with the hut behind; `hut` still passes.

## Loop pass 7 (2026-10-20) — seabird plunge dives

A seabird circling low over a school now strikes: once settled (`huntAmount` above 0.95) it
plunges every nine seconds for 1.6 s, a half-sine fold from its circling height to 0.35 m
above the water (the one time a bird may drop below its clearance; the vertical rate opens to
11 m/s for the plunge and the climb out), and at the bottom of the fold the flock records a
`BirdDiveSplash` (strike point and age, valid for 2.6 s). The ocean shader takes it as
`uBirdSplash` and draws a white plume at the strike that becomes a broken ring 1.8 times a
swimmer's splash radius, through the existing splash band. The startup log adds "circling
seabirds plunge-dive every nine seconds and each strike raises a foam ring on the water",
pinned by the native capture tool. The core seabird check now also requires a strike within a
minute of the low circling, within 24 m of the school. Native `birds` and `water` pass. A
splash sound is a candidate for a later pass.

## Loop pass 6 (2026-10-20) — boars wallow at the stream bank

The boars live on the vegetated banks of the western drainage corridor yet never entered it:
the stream corridor is the drainage field itself (0.96–0.97 at the bank against the habitat's
0.74 limit), and a probe showed every bank point otherwise valid. Each boar now finds, at
placement, the closest bank point a metre outside the channel within 0.9 of its range that
passes every habitat rule except drainage (`IsValidGround(x, z, allowDrainage)`); all six boars
have one. Steps onto drainage ground are allowed only for the new `Wallow` behaviour and for a
boar already standing on it (`BoarState::inChannel`, so one startled off its trip by the player
walks out instead of freezing), and ordinary foraging still keeps out of the corridor; the boar
herd test checks the strict habitat for every boar that is neither wallowing nor in the channel. Every third rest becomes a walk to the wallow at 0.5 m/s,
then fourteen seconds standing in the bank mud with the snout down (the rooting pose), facing
the water; `mudAmount` wets to 1 over six seconds there and dries off over 150 s afterwards.
The renderer paints the mud: the legs take 85 % of it and the body builder darkens the belly
and lower flanks (a height band below 0.52 m of the body frame) toward wet-mud brown while the
back stays dry. The wallow is quiet snuffling to the call scheduler. The ecology line now
reports "N boars wallow at the bank and carry the mud on their legs and bellies", pinned by the
native capture tool. New core check: at least one boar range reaches a bank, and within ten
simulated minutes a boar is wallowing with mud above 0.5 and reaches full mud. Native `boars`
passes.

## Loop pass 5 (2026-10-20) — gust fronts

The grass, crowns and fronds each swayed on their own two sines; nothing ever moved across the
island together. `WindGust` (shared GLSL and a CPU mirror) defines gust fronts: bands 140 m apart
travelling downwind (toward -x with the trade wind) at 6.5 m/s, so a front passes any point every
21.5 s, each front 11–42 m wide with soft edges and varying in strength across the wind (0.45–1)
through a slow sine. A gust never raises an amplitude: in each vertex shader the broad sway
blends toward a full downwind lean (`mix(broad, 1, 0.85 gust)`) and the detail sway eases by
40 %, so `jungleBroadWind + jungleDetailWind` and the grass and palm amplitudes stay as authored
and every collision and clearance envelope holds. The grass samples the gust at its blade's world
position, the canopy and palms at their instance position (`aInstance3.xz`). The startup log
adds "gust fronts sweep the grass, crowns and fronds downwind together every twenty-two seconds
within their authored sway", pinned by the native capture tool. New core checks on the CPU
mirror: a front passes a fixed point within half a minute and clears again, fronts repeat with
spacing over speed, and the front peaking at the origin peaks 20 m downwind about three seconds
later (a first draft travelled upwind and its first-sighting test was wrong for a periodic
field). Native `grass`, `palms`, `jungle` and `east` pass.

## Loop pass 4 (2026-10-20) — the high-tide wrack line

Real beaches carry the last high tide's strandings a few metres up the sand; ours ran clean
from the wet band to the dunes. The terrain material now lays a wrack line on the upper beach:
a band centred 5.4 m inland (full within 0.7 m, gone by 1.6 m), wandered by the broad and medium
fields (±2.6 m and ±0.6 m) and broken into drifts and gaps by a 5 m value-noise field (about
half the shoreline carries it), present only on sand above 0.12 m and within 26–64 m of the
camera. Inside it, shore-parallel dark weed strands (a value-noise field slow along the coast
arc and 6.5 cells/m across the shore distance, footprint-filtered), pale shell grit (a
2.4 cells/m fleck field) and a few darker twigs (0.65 cells/m) lie on sand that is itself 16 %
darker and damper. A magenta probe confirmed the band's place a few metres above the wet sand
before the strands were tuned to read at walking distance. The startup log adds "beaches carry a broken high-tide wrack line of
stranded weed, twigs and shell", pinned by the native capture tool. Inspected native
`20261019T222306Z-wet-sand` shows the broken dark line with its strands and grit a few metres
above the wet band; `beach`, `shipwreck-wide` and `hermit-crabs` pass their gates.

## Loop pass 3 (2026-10-20) — seabirds work the fish schools

The six seabirds only ever rode their high orbits 125–233 m out; a tropical shore shows them
working bait. `BirdFlock::SetSeaForage` takes the fish school of the moment (the game hands the
schools over in turn, ninety seconds each, so the circling moves around the coast), and every
75 s a seabird whose turn has come leaves its route for 42 s: it flies straight at the school
while more than three orbit radii away, then its orbit centre becomes the school with an 11 m
radius and a firmer radial pull, and its altitude blends (`huntAmount`,
ramping over two seconds so the dive and the climb back read as flight) from the route height
to 7.5 m above the water, never below four metres over the ground ahead; when the school is
withdrawn the hunts end and the island orbit's radial correction draws it back out. The
startup log adds "seabirds break from their high orbits to circle low over the fish school of
the moment", pinned by the native capture tool. New core check: given a school point 25 m off
the east shore, a seabird circles within 22 m of it below 14 m within four minutes (a first
draft with a 26 s hunt and a spiral approach never arrived in time), and no bird hunts once the
school is withdrawn. Native `birds` passes.

## Loop pass 2 (2026-10-20) — butterflies work the flowering bushes

The hibiscus and plumeria bushes added for backlog item 16 flower unvisited while the
clearing butterflies only ever hover over their ground flower patches; the clearings
themselves are bush-free (no bush lies within 12 m of any habitat centre; flowering ones sit
20–30 m out at the jungle edge). `ButterflyMeadow::SetFlowerBushes` now takes the jungle's
bushes and keeps up to six flowering ones (variants 1 and 2) within 24 m beyond each habitat's
radius as nectar sites (14 on this island), with a hover height just above the blossoms
(0.62 × scale + 0.30 m). Every other nectar bout of a butterfly whose habitat has sites goes to
one: a site beyond 3 m becomes an excursion, the butterfly flutters straight to it on a widened
range allowance (`reachRadius`, the site's distance from home plus 2.5 m), settles into the
hover at blossom height within a metre of it, and the allowance lapses once it has drifted back
inside its home range; nearer sites are hovered directly. The startup log reports "N flowering
bushes within reach of the habitats draw alternate nectar excursions at blossom height", pinned
by the native capture tool. New core check with synthetic bushes: only a flowering bush within
reach becomes a site, and a butterfly hovers at blossom height over it within two minutes.
Native `butterflies` passes.

## Loop pass 1 (2026-10-19/20) — dappled light on the shaded forest floor

With the twenty-item operator backlog complete, the open-ended propose-and-implement loop
began. First pass: the canopy's solid crowns cast one even shade, but real crowns leak sun
through leaf gaps as small bright flecks that drift as the leaves move. The terrain material now
derives `dappleShade` from the shadow-map/sky blend (how shaded the texel is) gated by the baked
crown field or the forest-floor mask, and within 30–70 m and a 3–10 cm footprint restores up to
95 % of the sunlit value where a two-octave drifting value-noise field (0.4 m and 0.17 m cells,
drift 0.11/0.07 m/s from `uSeaSeconds`) exceeds its threshold, so about a fifth of each crown
shadow is sun-flecked. The startup log adds "shaded forest floor carries drifting leaf-gap sun
flecks", pinned by the native capture tool. A forced-on probe confirmed the term reaches the
crown shade before the threshold was set. While here, the `ground` viewpoint's luminance gate
(failing since 2026-10-16 at 17.69 against the scene profile's 18.0, the sunlit close humus
simply has a narrow tonal range) is classified as close-natural-detail like its sibling close
views; it passes there. Inspected native `20261019T215850Z-jungle` shows the mottled flecks in
the crown shade; `litter`, `east` and `ground` pass.

## Latest diving pass — light shafts, bubbles and seabed caustics

Backlog item 20. `UnderwaterEffectRenderer` is a full-screen clip-space triangle drawn after
the water-view veil whenever the render camera is below the sea surface over seabed (camera
depth drives it, so the submerged QA cameras see it as a swimmer would): light shafts lean
toward the sun's side of the frame (the sun direction transformed into view space gives the
tilt, the facing and the height), brighten toward the top of the frame, fade with depth
(`exp(-0.16 d)`) and flicker through two slow carriers; while the player is actually swimming
(the veil intensity gates them) three lanes of ring-and-glint bubbles rise past the camera, and
a descent breathes out a burst that thins over two seconds (`bubbleBurst_` from the change in
`SubmergedDepth`). The pass adds light with zero coverage (premultiplied) so nothing darkens.
The terrain material gains `uSeaSeconds` and seabed caustics: two wavy line families
(`abs(sin)` warped by slow sines) cross into a bright net on ground 0.12–7.5 m below the surface,
footprint-filtered, strongest a metre down, lit by the ground light; it is visible from a diver
and through the surface from the beach. Diagnostics "underwater view adds sun-tilted light
shafts, the diver's rising bubbles and moving seabed caustics" and "shallow seabed carries
moving refracted-sun caustics that fade with depth and footprint", both pinned by the native
capture tool. Inspected native `20261019T215158Z-reef-habitat` shows the shafts from above,
bubbles and the caustic net around the coral; `reef` (from the surface), `tide-pools` and
`fish` pass their gates.

## Latest crossing pass — a rope bridge over the stream and plank footsteps

Backlog item 14 (the walkable member; the tree lookout stays open). `BridgeLayout::FindInWorld`
walks the stream stations from six past the plunge pool (or three fifths of the course,
whichever is later) toward the mouth and takes the first crossing whose anchors, 1.7 m outside
the channel on both banks, stand at least 0.24 m above the water (the right bank of the lower
reach sits only 0.27–0.30 m up), differ by no more than 0.6 m, slope less than 0.45 rad and are
not submerged, with the walkway's sagging middle still 0.18 m clear of the water; it lands at
station 59, a 5.3 m span. `BridgePlacement::DeckHeight` is linear between the anchors minus a
0.12 m parabolic sag; `SupportHeight` carries the walker across (after the stream bed patch and
the other structure supports) and `OnDeck` keeps them out of swimming mode like the jetty.
`BridgeRenderer` (932 triangles, one vertex-coloured draw, sun-shadow caster) draws planks
following the sag, two carrying ropes under the plank ends, two hand ropes on end posts and
vertical ties every 0.6 m; the per-face sun lighting now lives in a shared
`StructureMeshBuilder` that the jetty uses too. Walking on either deck now rings hollow:
`FootstepSurface::Wood` with a plank profile (short attack, lower resonant thump, little grit)
and two new clips (55 clips, 7,247,830 PCM bytes pinned). A `bridge` QA viewpoint stands on the
left bank looking across (close-natural-detail profile). The startup log adds "rope bridge
crosses the stream's lower reach on a sagging plank walkway with hand ropes; the walker crosses
dry", pinned by the native capture tool. New core checks: the site exists downstream of the
plunge pool, both anchors stand above the water, the walkway sags below its anchors but clears
the stream, and the support acts mid-span above the carved bed and nowhere beside the planks.
Inspected native `20261019T214605Z-bridge` shows the span with its ropes and ties over the
stream; `stream` still passes.

and ends over water, the deck supports the walker at its level height mid-span and leaves the

## Latest sea-from-within pass — leaping dolphins, a surface fin and parting schools

Backlog item 11. Dolphins gain a `Leap` behaviour: every fourth surfacing ends in a 1.5 s
ballistic arc driven directly (the ordinary 0.85 m/s vertical clamp would flatten it) that
crests 1.7 m above the surfacing depth at 3.6 m/s, with the pitch limit opened to 0.95 rad and
a faster pitch rate so the body follows the arc nose-up then nose-down; `LeapCount()` reports
leaps. The shark patrol rides nine seconds in every forty-six at a body depth of -0.85 m while
present, so the dorsal fin (tip 1.12 m above the body centre) and the tail cut the water; the
rest of the patrol stays at its former two-metre cruise, and the long-session depth check now
allows the finning window while still asserting the body stays below the surface. Fish schools
keep the swimmer's position: a fish within 3 m of the swimmer has its school slot pushed
straight away (1.8 m per metre of intrusion plus 0.6 m) and hurries at 1.7 times its speed, so
a school parts around a diver and closes behind. The startup log adds "sea from within:
dolphins leap clear of the water on every fourth surfacing, the shark shows its dorsal fin for
nine seconds of each patrol, and fish schools part around the swimmer within three metres",
pinned by the native capture tool; the overlay counts a leaping dolphin as surfacing. New core
checks: the pod leaps within five minutes with a crest above 0.9 m, and a school placed around
a swimmer at its centre parts to more than a metre. Native `dolphins`, `shark` and `fish`
captures pass.

pair walks back together; a sentinel lifts its head first and the others follow after 0.7 s",

observer 21 m beyond the deer sentinel the sentinel stands alert at once while its partner does

relaxes when the observer is gone. Native `goats` and `deer` captures pass.

## Latest ecology pass — drinking deer, rooting boars, fruit-picking monkeys

Backlog item 8. Deer and goats gain a `Drink` behaviour: at construction each animal searches
the authored stream route for the closest bank point (one metre outside the channel on its own
side) that its range and ground rules allow it to stand on; every other rest of a deer with such
a point, and every third of a goat, becomes a walk to the bank, where it faces the water and
holds the grazing head-down pose for the remainder of the bout. Both clearings lie 95–115 m
from the stream, so the fourth deer now keeps a stream-side range nine metres off the upper
reach instead of a second West-clearing home; it is the one drinker. The goat slopes are dry
upper ground far from the valley, so no goat qualifies on this island (the diagnostic reports
"1 deer and 0 goats"); moving a goat range toward the valley is a candidate for the loop.
Boars entering `Forage` choose the nearest trunk (a static obstacle of 0.12–1.6 m radius inside
their range) and a standing point just outside its collision envelope on valid ground, walk
there at 0.42 m/s and then stand with the snout toward the trunk, rooting among its surface
roots, for six extra seconds. Monkeys weight fruiting canopy forms (`IsFruitingCanopyVariant`,
variants 2 and 5, now shared with the renderer's fruit clusters) as 0.55 of their distance when
choosing a tree and hold their inspection nine seconds instead of six there (`pickingFruit`).
The startup log adds "ecological links: N deer and M goats walk to the stream bank to drink;
boars root at the nearest trunk base, monkeys favour fruiting crowns and linger to pick",
pinned by the native capture tool; the `boars` view joins the close-natural-detail profile
because the rooting boar now fills the frame with evenly lit ground. The goat contact-call
scheduler treats drinking as quiet hoof work. Inspected native `20261019T211710Z-boars` shows
the boar rooting; `deer` still frames the first clearing deer. Goat drinking remains unexercised
on this island.

rate scaled by walking speed) that thrusts the near head forward 5.5 cm and dips it, the pigeon
walk; it clears when the dove departs. A third dove palette, pigeon grey with a rose breast
and an iridescent green neck, joins the two fruit-dove greens. The audio inventory gains the

`20261019T205938Z-ground-doves` shows the grey pigeon-palette dove walking; `birds` still frames
the parrot. Human listening of the coo remains an operator check.

## Latest stream pass — a small cascade and plunge pool

Backlog item 6. `StreamCourse::ShapeCascade` finds the steepest three-metre run of the natural
water profile (outside the source reach and the mouth) and gathers it into one level lip and a
single drop between two stations (0.53 m at 47.4 m along the course), then deepens and widens
the seven stations below it into a plunge pool (up to 0.34 m extra depth within a 1.45 m
incision limit, up to 55 % wider), all through the existing station fields so the dense bed
patch and the water ribbon follow without new geometry paths. The water shader takes
`uCascade` (course distance, drop) and adds white water: a churning sheet over the lip, a plunge
below it and a foam raft the pool carries and dissolves over five metres. The cascade is also a
sound destination: `StreamSoundField::Sample` takes the lip as a second source that is heard to
58 m (the quiet reaches fade by 34 m), reports `turbulence`, and the stream voice gains up to
60 % and sits on the lip when the cascade dominates. A `cascade` QA viewpoint stands on the bank
below the pool looking up at the lip (close-natural-detail profile). Diagnostics "stream drops
N m over a small cascade at D m into a plunge pool with white water" and "stream cascade gathers
the steepest reach into one lip, a drop and a wider plunge pool" (pinned in the native `stream`
capture). New core checks: the cascade sits inside the course, drops at least 12 cm, the lip
holds level or at freeboard, the water never rises downstream, the pool incision stays within
its limit, the pool is deeper and wider than the reach above, and the cascade is turbulent up
close and audible further than the quiet reaches. Inspected native
`20261019T205523Z-cascade` shows the white sheet at the lip, the step and the wider pool with
leaf rafts; the `stream` capture and its four animation stages still pass.

## Latest beach-streak audit — seabed ripples confined below the waterline

Backlog item 4. The light/dark streaks converging over the whole foreground of the wide wreck
frame were bisected with frame-column shader probes (vertex colour only; then each procedural
block in turn): the per-vertex base is clean, the wind-ripple relief and the sun shadow map are
not the cause, and the one term that produced them is the seabed ripple, `sin(shoreDistance *
9.5)` under `seabedMask`. Its height mask `1 - smoothstep(-0.18, 0.02, y)` reached the exposed
flat at the tide line, so from a low camera looking along the beach its straight shore-parallel
crests (0.66 m) read as streaks for twenty metres. The mask now ends at -0.12 m (full below
-0.45 m), fades between 5 and 16 m, and runs in short trains through a 1.6 m field; the dry-sand
wind ripples likewise run in 2 m trains with a smaller slope (0.0017) and drop their relief
lighting by 24 m, and the pebble/shell fleck lattice, which has no mip chain, fades with the
ground footprint (0.018–0.060 m) instead of distance alone, on the beach and in the shallows.
The startup log adds "seabed ripples stay below the waterline in short near trains and beach
flecks fade with the ground footprint", pinned by the native capture tool. Inspected native
`20261019T204535Z-shipwreck-wide` keeps only the broad authored sand relief in the foreground;
`wet-sand`, `tide-pools` and `reef` pass their gates unchanged in character.

## Latest wreck-grounding pass — sand scour bar against the hull

Backlog item 3. The grounded ship sat on the untouched four-metre seabed grid, so its hull met
the shallows with no sign of the sand a grounded hull gathers. The dense-grid replacement that
carved the stream bed is now a shared base, `LocalTerrainPatch` (coarse range, subdivision and a
per-vertex height rule; untouched coarse cells stay fans in their original planes, changed cells
subdivide, boundary vertices keep their original height), with `StreamBedPatch` rebuilt on it
unchanged. `WreckScourPatch` is a second patch on that base: a one-metre grid within 16 m of the
ship whose rule raises an elliptical bar around the hull outline, a long drift tongue on the lee
(shoreward) side (crest 0.62 m, 5.2 m decay, capped at +0.22 m so it just breaks the surface) and a
short scour lip to seaward (0.30 m, 2.4 m decay, capped below the waterline), with a fixed-seed
ripple on the bar edge and a world-axis fade that reaches zero before the patch boundary. The
terrain renderer removes the covered coarse quads and draws the bar as a third replacement buffer
with the terrain material (1,482 vertices, 2,905 triangles), and `PlayerMotion` now consults both
patches for ground contact, so wading beside the hull stands on the bar. The height-based wet
band already shades the emerged tongue as wet sand. The startup log adds "wreck scour bar rises
on the lee side of the hull and stays submerged to seaward", pinned by the native capture tool.
New core checks: the patch covers the hull, boundary vertices keep the original height, the bar
never lowers the seabed, never exceeds the lee cap, breaks the surface beside the hull, stays
submerged to seaward and rises above the buried keel. Inspected native `20261019T203308Z-shipwreck-wide`
and `20261019T203317Z-shipwreck` show the hull in a pale bar with the drift tongue toward the beach.

## Latest cave overhead repair — real soil overburden instead of a covered tube

The operator's free-flight screenshot `Screenshot From 2026-10-17 15-48-44.png` correctly
contradicted the earlier completion language: although the rock crown had an earth colour, the
cave still read from above as a long freestanding tube in a trench, with two dark side channels
and a tall green outer rear cap. The fixed overhead QA view reproduced the defect. The first
attempt to narrow only the height-field excavation removed the rear cap but retained jagged side
gaps; a cave floor and a roof cannot both be represented by one height at the same X/Z.

`CaveGroundPatch` therefore now carries a second render-only, 57x49 terrain-material surface above
the unchanged low support grid. It follows the measured top of the closed collision shell with at
least 6.9cm clearance, spreads through an asymmetric 28m-wide soil shoulder, and rejoins the
original hillside behind and beside the cave. The terrain shader restricts its stone override by
height, so this upper layer receives ordinary forest-soil treatment while the lower traversable
floor remains stone. The same terrain draw now contains 6,270 vertices / 12,096 triangles. The
cave draw remains one batch; the five portal rocks and 20m interior are unchanged.

New regression checks reject a depressed side trench, an uncovered outer rear cap, non-finite or
undersized overburden, and any cover vertex dipping through the rock crown. The player still walks,
stops at the back, exits, flies against the inner roof, lands, and can stand on the covered upper
flank. `IslandCaveLayoutTests` plus all 55 capture/browser harness tests pass.
Inspected native evidence `20261017T140954.115032Z-cave-top`,
`20261017T141021.371835Z-cave`, and `20261017T141048.917010Z-cave-inside` passes the updated strict
gate. From above the rear wall, side trenches and exposed tube are gone; the result is a broad
vegetated hillside with an irregular rock opening. The operator visually approved this overhead
soil/terrain result on 2026-10-17, so that specific item is complete. WebGL/Android rebuild and

## Latest terrain visual-audit implementation — distance-stable coastal cliff strata

The overview/headland/east comparison selected the low coastal cliff because its existing close
bedding and joints correctly filtered away at distance, leaving the full seven-metre face as one
grey curtain. The coastal-only material branch now retains gently warped metre-scale strata,
restrained warmer mineral beds and irregular vertical drainage streaks. A low-amplitude final
modulation survives the far outcrop blend; a stronger intermediate was inspected and rejected as
artificially striped.

The change adds one low-frequency value-noise sample and bounded sine/blend arithmetic only on
steep rocky fragments. Geometry, collision, terrain cells, textures and draw count are unchanged.

native baseline `20261016T213030.275073Z-headland` and accepted

## Latest visual-audit implementation — rounded goat barrel and joint masses

The refreshed overview and bear/boar/goat comparison selected the goat as the weakest ordinary
large-animal silhouette. Its detailed barrel now uses sixteen radial sections instead of twelve,
with eight rather than six in the far tier. Revised longitudinal rings lift the waist underside,
retain distinct rounded haunch and shoulder masses and slope the topline into the neck. The coat's
physical-height projection expands to 0.70 m so the taller outline does not clamp or swim.

Existing planted leg targets, support normals and split hooves are unchanged. Larger upper-limb,
knee and hock rings plus a stronger bounded intermediate offset make the articulated chain read as
an animal leg rather than a straight rod. Near/far inventories become exactly 8,160/4,416 vertices;
six all-near animals use 48,960 vertices below the unchanged 49,152 batch capacity, still in two
draws. Goat mesh/herd/habitat/world-report/core and all 103 browser/capture harness tests pass.

luminance deviation and 254.51 spatial contrast. Focused Chrome/SwiftShader

## Latest visual-audit implementation — rounded butterfly body and legs

The current close-animal audit selected the butterfly because its otherwise recognisable patterned
wings still surrounded a pointed, arrow-like dark body. The near mesh now carries a fourth

pairs of legs, a rounder two-stage forewing shoulder, and a small local wing marking in place of
the long root-to-centre triangle. The result reads as an insect rather than a coloured paper dart
in the live overhead inspection.

## Latest operator priorities — 2026-10-12

Target-window constraint: aim to implement all still-open work inside approximately 100 productive
hours, continue working after that boundary unless the operator stops the campaign, and accept extra
hours if the operator extends the budget.
Do not silently remove requested features. Give every retained feature a functional, recognisable,
integrated implementation, but reduce visual ambition to the smallest coherent version: generally
one model/material treatment, one motion set, bounded procedural detail and one targeted visual
iteration. Photorealism, numerous bespoke animation/model variants, extensive texture passes and
repeated cross-platform art tuning follow the functional pass or fill time saved by finishing it early.
Crash fixes, input correctness, traversal safety, deterministic placement, bounded simulation/render
cost and representative native runtime evidence keep their normal acceptance bar. Portable Web and
Android work is consolidated around affected subsystems and final integration rather than repeated
per-feature polish passes.

Working allocation for the target 100-hour implementation window (re-estimate after each integrated stage):

- 10 h — stability, controls, fly/dive boundaries and regression work;
- 20 h — wildlife counts, habitat, motion and missing animal audio;
- 12 h — recognisable visual repairs for existing animals and aquatic wildlife;
- 10 h — stream biome, local ambience and remaining low-cost ecosystem links;
- 14 h — inland hut, small cave and campfire landmarks;
- 14 h — one resident and one bear with bounded movement/audio;
- 12 h — grounded enterable helicopter at reduced visual-detail target;
- 8 h — integration, performance budgets, portable smoke coverage and release buffer.

These are control budgets, not permission to leave a feature half-connected or to stop when the
window is consumed: simplify geometry/material/animation variety before cutting required behavior,
then keep improving remaining or shallow items until the operator ends the work.

Build constraint: all future compilations are limited to at most three CPU cores
by explicit user request (reduced from four on 2026-10-14). Use `-j3` / `--parallel 3`
or fewer workers, bound nested tool workers, and serialize builds. Where tools use
internal threads, restrict the build process tree to at most three allowed logical
CPUs. This supersedes older uncapped and four-worker guidance; the Android wrapper's
existing two-worker limit remains suitable.

  actual close approach, and guard against body/foot sliding introduced by slower heading changes.

  and snakes (1.8 rad/s articulated retreat), but deer directly replaced their body heading both
  on observer avoidance and failed ground moves. Deer now retain a target heading, turn at a
  species-appropriate 1.45 rad/s retreat / 0.92 rad/s ordinary limit, and reduce forward speed
  while badly misaligned so the slower turn does not create lateral foot sliding. The deterministic
  close-observer regression measures every frame and rejects any heading jump beyond that bound;
  deer plus goat/boar/bear/crocodile/snake motion suites pass. Inspected native capture
  `20261017T124807.997479Z-deer` preserves the planted, readable silhouette. Monkey retreat now uses
  a 1.65 rad/s ceiling and 4.2 rad/s² angular acceleration, slows forward travel while the torso is
  misaligned, and applies the same bounded steering while deflecting around obstacles. Its dedicated
  120-frame close-observer regression rejects both rate and acceleration spikes; the full core suite

- [~] 2026-10-19 operator report: mouse look on the Web build needs far more mouse travel than
  the desktop. The game applies one `MouseSensitivity` (0.0021 rad per unit) to SDL relative
  motion; on the desktop SDL delivers raw relative counts, while the browser pointer lock delivers
  OS-accelerated CSS pixels divided by the device pixel ratio, so one physical sweep yields far
  fewer units. The Web build now multiplies mouse look by `MouseLookScale = 2.5`, and the release
  shell requests `unadjustedMovement` pointer lock (raw motion where Chrome offers it, with the
  plain lock as fallback). The exact ratio depends on the operator's mouse DPI and display
  scaling, so the factor must be confirmed in the real browser; automated SwiftShader runs cannot
  measure physical mouse travel.

## Resolved native frame-rate regression

`[x]` Operator confirms the Release version holds approximately 59.3 FPS. Runtime
`island-runtime-3558619.log` corroborates roughly 59 FPS during both walking and flight.
Keep the current native-performance profile and use Release for ordinary play; no further
quality reduction is justified by this incident. The earlier evidence below is historical.

Configuration follow-up: the operator was playing the unoptimized Debug binary in `build/`.
The stale native Release tree is now refreshed at `build-consumer/island-simulator`, keeping
the same quality/populations. Serial Release/Debug/Release CPU probes reduce the ground snake
update from 2.8509ms Debug to 0.4035/0.8606ms Release, with host variation; this is not an FPS
claim. Core/spider/snake/terrain Release tests pass 4/4, software jungle capture passes. Runtime
logs identify configuration and the capture gate checks it. Use Release for further hardware
walking feedback before cutting more quality; keep Debug available for development.

CPU follow-up: the 200-spider dormant tier was still replaying up to fifteen IK/terrain steps
per resident. At the user's recorded flight position this cost 3.372ms per simulation update with
no visible spiders. True suspension removes that work (0.0211ms in the CPU-only diagnostic), with
explicit all-resident wake-up/retained-foot regression coverage. Cached snake radii and an exact
constant-time terrain-cell lookup reduce repeated scalar work. Ordinary play now logs five-second
`frame-window` FPS/update/draw summaries and four wildlife update costs. The operator now reports
60 FPS high flight / 30 FPS walking. Their new live log confirms 55–56 FPS high-flight averages,
but walking varies 18–45 FPS. A 29.443 FPS walking window spends 16.532ms/frame updating and
16.563ms submitting draws; snakes alone take 4.188ms/update (spiders 0.590ms). Next investigate
snake CPU work and dense near-ground rendering; retain all 50 snakes / 200 spiders. No matched
same-route FPS measurement from before the population expansion exists.

The intermediate Debug retest only confirmed partial recovery. The earlier retained interactive
log shows 339 submitted frames in 15.95s before flight (about
21 FPS) and 143 frames in 13.83s during flight (about 10 FPS), despite an idle host. The renderer
was real AMD hardware, not llvmpipe, using the former full profile with 4x MSAA.

The first corrective pass removes the unrequested per-grass-vertex search through animated snake
segments, staggers reduced-tier snake simulation, and stops distant snake motion from rebuilding
the shared contact-shadow batch. A new native-performance profile keeps all populations and close
models but uses a 72m grass cutoff, 55% palm/jungle range, 50% shadow range, 70% wildlife range,
a 96x96 ocean grid and single-sample rendering. Web keeps the full profile and Android keeps its
mobile profile. The elevated llvmpipe overview first draw fell from 311.281ms to 200.735ms while
rendering the expanded current world; this is directional evidence, not an AMD frame-rate claim.
Core, snake, software-supervisor tests and native jungle/overview captures pass. The final
operator Release retest closes this FPS incident, not the unrelated AMD recovery investigation.

## Previous visual-audit implementation — fuller low-shrub structure

shoot spread earlier, adds a slightly stronger crooked bend, widens and lengthens its leaves, and
uses more varied pitch, cupping and pigment. The wood/foliage palette was also lifted enough for the
branch hierarchy and overlapping leaf planes to remain legible in shade. The deterministic 581
placements, leaf count, renderer batching, LOD identity and draw budget are unchanged.

A 2026-10-15 follow-up removes the remaining horizontal-shelf look: every existing leaf now has
bounded deterministic roll around its own longitudinal axis and carries its cup/normal in that
frame. Native A/B, Chrome/SwiftShader and ARM64 build/lint pass without count, buffer, texture or
draw changes. See `docs/shrub-structure.md`.

`build-consumer/software-captures/20261014T040512.273894Z-bush` and
`20261014T051902.262185Z-bush`. The accepted result has a broader lower silhouette, visible crooked
branching and less repetitive leaf planes without turning the shrub into a bright focal prop. A

`build/browser-software/20261014T052141.486387Z-chrome-bushes`, including the actual generated shrub

## Product definition and non-goals

`island-simulator` is a peaceful first-person tropical island walking and near-shore swimming
experience. Its approximately 500 m island is interesting because of terrain composition,
vegetation, wildlife, water, light, motion, sound, and polished traversal. It has no quests,
missions, combat, enemies, inventory, crafting, survival meters, economy, score, progression,
multiplayer, story campaign, dynamic weather, or day/night cycle.

The required release targets are:

| Target | Renderer | Minimum release evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Linux desktop | OpenGL 3.3 | Clean build plus repeated real-GPU play sessions |
| Web browser | WebGL 2 | Clean Emscripten build plus an actual supported-browser play session |
| Android | OpenGL ES 3 | Clean Android build plus a real device or emulator play session with touch input |

Compilation is not runtime validation. A target stays unverified until it has run in its intended
environment.

## Non-negotiable engineering constraints

- Use C++23.
- Consume current CNA `next` and current Sharp Runtime `next` only.
- Never edit CNA or Sharp Runtime source, worktrees, branches, indexes, or repository metadata.
- Keep framework workarounds in this repository, narrowly scoped and cross-referenced from
  `BUGS.md` when they address a confirmed framework defect.
- Use no more than eight CPU jobs. Use no more than two jobs for any operation governed by Sharp
  Runtime's stricter repository policy.
- Use the shared ccache at `/rv/cnaccache` with `CCACHE_BASEDIR=/rv`; never create another cache.
- Reuse only the approved build directory names: `build/`, `build-probe/`, `build-consumer/`,
  `build-asan/`, `build-ubsan/`, and `build-tsan/`.
- Never build in `/tmp` and never retain obsolete large generated artifacts.
- Prefer CNA/XNA abstractions and supported CNA extensions over raw OpenGL, SDL, or a new engine.
- Keep simulation and placement deterministic when this improves tests, debugging, and captures.
- Preserve a playable build at meaningful milestones; do not accumulate large untested batches.

look noticeably closer to reality. This applies to **existing and all future content**. Stylized,
cartoon-like or crude assets are defects to be fixed, not an accepted art direction. The operator
explicitly named the sea turtle as very poor ("really terrible"); it is the first known example,
not the only one.

Macro-geography realism backlog from the operator-supplied analysis (full Czech original kept
outside the repository at `../island_improvements.md`). Operator decision: **monkeys and wild boars
stay on the island** (treat them as introduced populations; do not remove them). The analysis'
main finding: the island needs stronger macro structure more than more micro detail; from above it
still reads as a flat procedural green oval inside a uniform sand ring. Suggested order and rough
effort, all within the peaceful fixed-daytime product and existing renderers:

- [~] 1. Rewrite `IslandTerrain` into an asymmetric, eroded small volcanic island with a fringing
  reef, keeping the ~500 m extent: an irregular main ridge with a 35-45 m summit, a 25-30 m second
  peak and saddle, valleys draining to the coast, 2-3 rocky headlands, one sheltered bay, one
  dominant sandy beach and one wilder rocky side (15-20 h). Re-place every existing system on it.
  2026-10-11 interior stage: 40/29 m ridges, lower saddle, two drainage cuts, weathered
  steep faces and terrain-aware bird clearance (`docs/ridge-and-valleys.md`). The next stage
  added a western bay and three headland silhouettes (`docs/coastal-silhouette.md`);
  rocky coastal relief and the shared environment remain open. Android lifecycle has an intermittent
  `EGL_BAD_SURFACE` issue documented separately in `BUGS.md`.
- [~] 2. Replace the uniform beach ring with distinct coast types: leeward wide calm beach
  (palms, wreck, driftwood, turtles), windward rocky/reef coast with larger waves, more foam and
  wind-shaped low vegetation, and a sheltered turquoise bay; vegetation reaching the water in places;
  reef flats (10-15 h).
- [~] 3. Add a shared `IslandEnvironmentField` (moisture, salt/wind/wave exposure, soil depth,
  rockiness, drainage, sun exposure, reef suitability) and drive palms, canopy, shrubs, ferns,
  grass and props from it instead of concentric `signedShoreDistance` bands (10-15 h). The current
  ground-cover field is a first step and should become one of its inputs.
- [~] 4. One prevailing trade wind (for example from the east) used consistently: palm lean and
  crown shape, windward ocean/foam, rock exposure, vegetation height, driftwood accumulation, dune
  orientation, cloud wisps and wind audio. 2026-10-10 first pass (`docs/prevailing-wind.md`):
  shared east trade wind, coastal windward exposure, palms lean up to ten degrees; tested;
  native palms/beach/overview captures inspected. Driftwood and cloud/wisp direction now
  consume the shared wind; ocean, foam, crowns and audio remain.
- [~] 5. Make the reef readable from a distance: seabed macro structure with a pale lagoon, sand
  channels, dark reef patches and seagrass, a reef crest and a deep blue drop-off, before any
  detailed coral models. The existing terrain material now uses four explicit broad cues: a pale
  6–48m lagoon retaining radial sand channels, reef patches modulated by the same angular field as
  CPU coral/fauna placement, a broken 62–86m crest and restrained 78m+ blue-green drop-off. The
  former rock-obscured QA camera is now an elevated wide shelf composition. Inspected native

  and stones instead of a ~12 m corridor that visibly halves the island from above.

## Architectural decisions

### Dependency identity and read-only consumption

The build must reject an accidental non-`next` dependency. Because the only CNA working tree is on
`samples` and may not be switched or modified, initial Linux work will use a reproducible,
unmodified export of the exact CNA `next` tree under the ignored `build/` area, or an externally
provided read-only CNA `next` worktree. The source export is build input, never vendored or edited
game code. CMake will receive explicit roots for CNA, Sharp Runtime, EasyGL, and MetaGL and record
their resolved identities in configure output. Normal developer documentation will recommend
separate sibling checkouts on their required branches.

### Runtime boundary

Game code uses the XNA-shaped `Microsoft::Xna::Framework` API and only narrowly justified CNA
extensions. Raw OpenGL/GLES/WebGL and native SDL calls are prohibited in gameplay/rendering code.
This protects renderer portability and makes framework limitations explicit.

### World representation

The island uses a finite terrain mesh/height field suited to a roughly 500 m landmass, not a
planet-scale terrain engine. A deterministic authored-procedural hybrid provides repeatable base
terrain, biome/density maps, authored landmarks, clearings, paths, coves, rock groups, and spawn
regions. Height, normal, slope, shoreline distance, biome, and navigability queries share one
authoritative CPU representation so rendering, collision, placement, wildlife, and tests agree.

### Rendering strategy

Start with portable CNA vertex/index buffers and stock effects. Use static batching and CNA's
instancing where verified on all required renderers. Near grass uses compact mesh clusters with
vertex wind; middle/far grass reduces density and complexity. Avoid geometry, tessellation, and
compute shaders. Fixed sunny lighting permits precomputed ambient/occlusion information and stable
shadow choices. Expensive desktop-only effects must have deliberate Web/mobile fallbacks.

### Content strategy

Prefer original procedural meshes/textures/audio and redistributable CC0/public-domain inputs.
Every external asset is copied into the reproducible asset pipeline and entered in
`ASSET_LICENSES.md` before use. Runtime assets are generated deterministically where practical;
source assets remain available when licensing permits.

### Simulation strategy

Player and wildlife simulation run at bounded fixed steps with interpolated presentation where
useful. Wildlife shares a lightweight state/steering framework with species-specific constraints.
Distance tiers suspend or reduce invisible simulation. The ocean limit is a soft, island-relative
current field followed by an emergency recovery only beyond a second safety radius.

## Cross-platform rendering contract

Portable baseline:

- GLES 3.0 / WebGL 2 compatible vertex/fragment functionality.
- 16-bit indices where practical; split large batches rather than assuming unrestricted meshes.
- Bounded uniform/bone palettes and texture units.
- Mipmapped compressed or sensibly sized uncompressed textures with explicit fallbacks.
- Stock CNA effects first; custom shaders are authored from one semantic source or kept in a small,
  explicitly equivalent profile set.
- No geometry, tessellation, or compute shader dependency.
- No raw API capability query scattered through gameplay code; centralize feature/quality policy.

Expected scalable differences:

| Feature | Linux OpenGL 3.3 | WebGL 2 | Android GLES 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grass density/distance | Full, 135 m | Full, 135 m | Same density/near mesh, 112 m maximum |
| Dynamic shadows | Portable contact batch, full range | Same full range | Same batch, 72% range |
| Ocean detail | Full layers, 160 by 160 grid | Same layers/grid | Same layers, 128 by 128 grid |
| Wildlife range/count | Full | Full | Same counts/simulation, 82% draw range |
| Texture/audio sizes | 143,624 bytes / six sources | Same bounded inventory | Same bounded inventory |

Any larger difference must be added to the renderer-differences documentation and accepted only
after the same experience remains available.

## Asset pipeline and licensing gates

- No external asset enters a runtime build before source, author, license, modifications, and use
  are recorded in `ASSET_LICENSES.md`.
- Store reproducible source and conversion settings; do not depend on an asset remaining online.
- Do not commit temporary archives, duplicate conversions, source-control-hostile build products,
  or unlicensed placeholders.
- Procedural outputs use stable seeds and can be regenerated.
- Model validation includes scale, axes, normals/tangents, UVs, material slots, skeleton, clip names,
  bounds, and all renderer fallbacks.
- Audio validation includes sample rate/channels, loop boundaries, normalization, license, and
  spatial suitability.

## Test and runtime evidence matrix

| System | Automated evidence | Runtime evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Terrain | Query, normal, slope, deterministic generation tests | Walk every biome and boundary |
| Player | Integration, collision, water transition, water-view fade tests | Feel/tuning sessions at varied frame rates |
| Ocean limit | Distance/current invariants and escape scenarios | Repeated outward swims from multiple shores |
| Placement | Seed/golden counts, slope/biome validity | Pop-in, repetition, collision, composition review |
| Wildlife | State, bounds, spawn, deterministic tests | Observe all species near/far for long loops |
| Animation | Clip/state/palette validity tests | Transition and renderer comparison captures |
| Audio | Config/attenuation/zone logic tests | Headphone/speaker walk-through and long-loop review |
| Assets | Manifest/load/config parsing tests | Missing/corrupt asset diagnostic smoke tests |
| Renderers | Build/shader/package checks | Linux GPU, actual browser, Android device/emulator |

## Risk register

| Risk | Likelihood / impact | Mitigation and trigger |
|---|---|---|
| CNA checkout is not on `next` | Current / high | Exact-commit read-only export or separate read-only worktree; configure rejects mismatch |
| Upstream branch movement breaks build | Medium / high | Record commits, update deliberately, run all active workaround regressions |
| CNA consumer integration assumes repository root | Known / medium | Use isolated game-side CMake adapters; document confirmed defects in `BUGS.md` |
| Web shader/runtime parity gaps | Medium / high | Use shared portable baseline early; actual browser milestone before content is final |
| Android lifecycle/input differences | Medium / high | Integrate package/touch shell before final content; test pause/resume early |
| Grass overdraw and draw calls | High / high | Cell batching/instancing, opaque/masked geometry, aggressive LOD, profile worst views |
| Dense jungle impairs traversal | High / medium | Authored paths/clearings, collision-light small plants, repeated route tests |
| Ocean edge feels like an invisible wall | Medium / high | Multi-stage current/resistance/feedback field and test from diverse shore normals |
| Legal monkey/animal assets unavailable | Medium / medium | Prefer original/simple legal substitute, document replacement path, never use dubious assets |
| Skeletal animation differs by renderer | Medium / high | Validate one small asset on all three paths before building monkey behaviour around it |
| Audio loops become fatiguing | High / medium | Long beds, layered random events, cooldowns, 20+ minute listening passes |
| Scope grows into general engine work | Medium / high | Keep island-specific systems explicit; reject features outside product definition |
| Disk growth from cross-builds/assets | Medium / medium | Measure periodically, reuse approved trees, delete only owned superseded artifacts |

### 2026-10-07 — Portable persistent player preferences

- Added schema-1 `UserSettings` parsing/serialization and a CNA `StorageDevice`-backed
  `UserSettingsStore`. Ordinary launches now restore the selected Shift walk/run pace, B camera-
  motion state, M mute state, and Android low/standard/high touch-look response. The parser is
  deliberately bounded and rejects oversize or NUL-containing input, duplicate or missing current
  keys, unsupported schemas, and invalid values while ignoring documented future keys.
- Settings use the platform-native CNA container (`settings.ini`, a last-valid backup, and a
  temporary replacement): XDG user storage on Linux, IDBFS with automatic persistence on Web, and
  app-private storage on Android. Smoke, capture, benchmark, and fixed-view QA launches are
  isolated automatically; `--no-user-settings` provides explicit isolation. Load/save diagnostics
  are mirrored to Android logcat. The implementation is entirely game-owned and no dependency
  source was changed.
- Added core round-trip/malformed-input tests plus `IslandGameSettingsPersistence`, which launches
  three real native sessions under an isolated XDG root: the first writes exact toggles, the second
  restores them, and the third corrupts the primary file and recovers the valid backup. Increased
  synthetic key dwell times for slow frames and taught native input tests to reuse CNA's private
